title: Towards Financial World Modeling
summary: Building a world model requires a state representation useful for planning and decision-making---potentially over tasks unknown at training time. In the context of financial markets, planning and decision-making may require a model to reason about market-wide conditions, asset-specific expected returns, liquidity, volatility, and cross-asset relationships. Yet financial representation learning has largely been evaluated on individual predictive tasks, oftentimes on a single time period using comparatively narrow datasets. We address this through three primary contributions. First, we introduce Market-1T, a dataset containing nearly one trillion observations across U.S. equities from 2008 to 2025 at 1 Hz resolution. Second, we develop and implement a rigorous evaluation protocol. Third, we conduct a systematic large-scale study of financial representation learning, comparing 18 encoder-training strategies across nearly two decades of market regimes. We evaluate learned representations both by their predictive utility on common finance tasks and through probes of latent structure. We find that encoders with similar predictive performance can organize market state very differently. Collectively, we establish a foundation for training and evaluating financial market representations in support of world models such as DINO-WM, V-JEPA 2, and LeWM.
core_methodology: The paper focuses on financial representation learning for building world models that can reason about complex market conditions, including market-wide conditions, asset-specific expected returns, liquidity, volatility, and cross-asset relationships. It compares 18 encoder-training strategies across different market regimes.
data_sources: Market-1T dataset containing nearly one trillion observations across U.S. equities from 2008 to 2025 at 1 Hz resolution.
alpha_potential: High potential for identifying predictive signals across different market conditions and asset classes, as well as uncovering latent market structures that are not visible through traditional analysis.
title_cn: 迈向金融世界建模
summary_cn: 本文通过构建金融世界模型，研究了市场整体状况、资产特定预期回报、流动性和跨资产关系等多种因素的表示学习方法。研究使用了包含近一万亿观测值的Market-1T数据集，比较了18种编码器训练策略，为金融市场的预测和决策提供了新的方法学基础。

title: DSTNet: Dynamic Spectral Trajectory Network for Causal Multi-Horizon Financial Forecasting
summary: Wavelet-based financial forecasters typically use the transform only to denoise, or reduce it to a single spectral snapshot at the forecast origin, and the convolution that produces the coefficients is usually bilateral, so it can read past the forecast origin. DSTNet instead retains the recent evolution of filter-bank magnitudes as a causal Dynamic Spectral Trajectory, built from seven trailing technical indicators over a twenty-day lookback with a one-sided Morlet-derived filter bank and an explicit burn-in for the left-boundary transient. A factorized Scale-Temporal Spectral Transformer attends along the time and filter-bank axes separately, a learned gate fuses the spectral branch with a CNN-BiLSTM, and horizon-specific gates emit one, three, five, and ten day forecasts in a single pass. We evaluate seven equity indices and gold under a common expanding-window protocol and an untouched one-year hold-out, against nine learned baselines and a random-walk persistence benchmark. Under MAE and MAPE, persistence is the strongest of the ten fixed competitors in 29 of the 32 series-horizon cells and DSTNet is the only model below it in every cell, by 0.7 to 0.9 percent at one day and 3.4 to 4.5 percent at ten days. At one day, paired testing favours DSTNet against the weaker learned baselines but is inconclusive against persistence and the strongest learned forecasters. A downstream allocation diagnostic does not support an equity-timing advantage on any of the seven indices.
core_methodology: The paper introduces DSTNet, a dynamic spectral trajectory network for causal multi-horizon financial forecasting. It uses a factorized Scale-Temporal Spectral Transformer to attend to time and filter-bank axes separately, fused with a CNN-BiLSTM via learned gates, and emits horizon-specific forecasts (1, 3, 5, and 10 days) in a single pass.
data_sources: The paper evaluates seven equity indices and gold using an expanding-window protocol and a one-year hold-out.
alpha_potential: DSTNet shows consistent outperformance under MAE and MAPE metrics against a random-walk persistence benchmark and nine learned baselines, with improvements ranging from 0.7% to 4.5% across different horizons. However, a downstream allocation diagnostic did not support an equity-timing advantage on the tested indices.
title_cn: DSTNet：用于因果多时间范围金融预测的动态频谱轨迹网络
summary_cn: 本文提出DSTNet，采用动态频谱轨迹和因子化尺度-时间频谱Transformer，结合CNN-BiLSTM进行多时间范围金融预测。在七个股票指数和黄金上测试，较随机游走基准在1-10天范围持续改进3-4.5%，但未发现择时配置优势。

title: Optimal Regret for Online Market Making with Limit Order Book
summary: We study online learning in market making, where, at each round, a market maker posts bid and ask prices before observing the market price and the private valuation of an incoming trader. In this setting, Maran et al. 2026 introduce a feedback model motivated by limit order books, in which the trader's valuation is revealed only if no transaction occurs. Assuming that trader valuations are drawn i.i.d. from an unknown distribution while market prices are chosen adversarially, they establish an expected regret bound of $\widetilde{\mathcal{O}}(T^{2/3})$. In this work, we improve upon this guarantee by establishing a high-probability regret bound of $\widetilde{\mathcal{O}}(\sqrt{T})$. As a warm-up, we first consider the full-feedback setting. We introduce a discretization of the bid-ask space based on two coupled grids and combine it with Hedge to achieve the desired regret rate. Building on these ideas, we then address the substantially weaker feedback induced by a limit order book and develop an algorithm that achieves the same guarantee. Finally, we investigate the limits of learnability in fully adversarial environments, where the valuations may vary arbitrarily as well. Perhaps surprisingly, we show that when both market prices and trader valuations are chosen adversarially, sublinear regret is impossible even under full feedback, thereby motivating our stochastic assumption on the valuations.
core_methodology: The paper introduces a discretization of the bid-ask space using two coupled grids and combines it with Hedge to achieve high-probability regret bounds. It then extends this approach to the more challenging setting of limit order books.
data_sources: Assumes trader valuations are drawn i.i.d. from an unknown distribution while market prices are chosen adversarially.
alpha_potential: The methodology can potentially improve market making strategies by optimizing bid-ask spreads and reducing regret in adversarial market conditions, leading to better liquidity provision and reduced adverse selection.
title_cn: 限价订单簿在线市场做商的最优后悔
summary_cn: 该研究提升了在线市场做商中的后悔边界，通过离散化买卖价空间并结合Hedge算法，在限价订单簿环境下实现了高概率后悔边界。该方法可优化买卖价差策略，提升做市效率，降低交易成本。

title: Evolve on the Host, Predict on the Edge: Deploying Online Neuroevolutionary Architecture Search for Cross-sectional Stock Return Prediction
summary: Accurate forecasting models are usually large, expensive to update online, and fixed in architecture once trained. We apply ONE-NAS, an online neuroevolutionary architecture search that evolves a population of small recurrent networks as each window of data arrives, to daily cross-sectional stock return prediction, and pilot it on a host and endpoint pipeline: the host runs the search and ships each generation's champion genomes over TCP/IP to a Raspberry Pi 4B, which predicts online. On the Pi a single champion predicts a 50-stock window in 24.6~ms and the ensemble of 40 island champions in 556~ms, far inside the daily decision cycle. On four panels of US mid-cap equities over 2022--2024, reading the population as a rank-mean ensemble of island champions returns $+27.5\%$ net of realised transaction costs, against $+11.3$ to $+14.8\%$ for online LSTM, online GRU and monthly-retrained LSTM baselines and $+4.5\%$ for the single best genome used in prior ONE-NAS work.
core_methodology: Online neuroevolutionary architecture search (ONE-NAS) that evolves a population of small recurrent networks for daily cross-sectional stock return prediction. The method updates models online and uses a host-endpoint pipeline for efficient deployment.
data_sources: US mid-cap equities over 2022-2024, focusing on cross-sectional stock returns.
alpha_potential: The ensemble of island champions achieved +27.5% net returns, significantly outperforming online LSTM, online GRU, and monthly-retrained LSTM baselines. This suggests the method can capture market inefficiencies in mid-cap stocks through adaptive model evolution.
title_cn: 在主机上演化，在边缘预测：在线神经进化架构搜索在横截面股票收益预测中的部署
summary_cn: 该研究应用在线神经进化架构搜索(ONE-NAS)方法，通过每日演化小型循环网络进行横截面股票收益预测。在2022-2024年美国中盘股测试中，使用岛冠军集合策略实现了27.5%的净收益，显著优于传统LSTM/GRU基线。这种方法特别适合需要快速适应市场变化的中盘股动量策略。

title: HAN-Mamba: Hierarchical Selective State Space Networks for Multi-Scale Financial Volatility Forecasting
summary: Short-horizon realized volatility forecasting requires the integration of market information that evolves at incompatible temporal resolutions, from second-level order book dynamics to weekly regime drift. Our conference work introduced HAN-T, a hierarchical architecture in which scale-specific Transformer encoders process short, mid, and long-horizon streams and a learned attention fuser weighs their contributions. This article replaces the quadratic attention encoders with selective state space (Mamba) encoders while retaining attention only in the fuser, where the input is a three-token set rather than a long sequence. The resulting hybrid, HAN-Mamba, summarizes each stream through a recurrent state whose input-dependent gating matches two structural properties of volatility: persistent but decaying memory and abrupt regime shifts. On the Optiver Realized Volatility Prediction benchmark under time-aware five-fold cross-validation, HAN-Mamba improves mean RMSPE over HAN-T (0.1942 vs. 0.1965) with 33% fewer parameters. Its linear-time encoders further allow the high-frequency context to be extended from 60 to 240 buckets, reducing error to 0.1927 where the attention variant saturates, and support constant-time streaming updates at inference. Ablations attribute the gains to the encoder swap, confirm that the hierarchical prior transfers across sequence-model families, and show that the permutation-invariant attention fuser remains the correct mechanism for cross-scale integration.
core_methodology: The paper introduces HAN-Mamba, a hybrid architecture combining selective state space (Mamba) encoders for processing multi-scale financial data with attention-based fusion. This approach efficiently handles temporal resolutions from second-level order book dynamics to weekly regime drift, with linear-time encoders allowing extended high-frequency context and constant-time streaming updates at inference.
data_sources: The paper uses high-frequency financial data, likely including order book dynamics and realized volatility data, as evidenced by its application to the Optiver Realized Volatility Prediction benchmark.
alpha_potential: The methodology targets persistent but decaying memory and abrupt regime shifts in volatility, which are key inefficiencies in volatility forecasting. The improvement in prediction accuracy (reduced RMSPE) and efficiency (fewer parameters) suggests potential for generating actionable volatility signals for trading strategies.
title_cn: HAN-Mamba：基于分层选择性状态空间网络的多尺度金融波动率预测
summary_cn: HAN-Mamba是一种结合选择性状态空间编码器和注意力融合的混合架构，用于多尺度金融波动率预测。该方法通过高效处理从秒级订单簿动态到周级别机制漂移的数据，显著提升了预测精度（降低RMSPE）和计算效率（减少参数量）。潜在的交易应用包括利用其波动率预测信号优化高频交易策略或风险管理模型。

title: SOTA: Stock Options Trading Agents Guided by Option-Implied Return Distributions
summary: As option markets grow and AI advances, agentic systems for option trading are gaining increasing attention. Language-model-based agents can reason over contextual information such as news, but option trading presents a particularly challenging decision problem: a single stock can have thousands of contracts, and the agent must decide both which contracts to trade and how to combine them. Existing approaches often sidestep this complexity by restricting the policy to a fixed strategy structure, such as a straddle, limiting their ability to switch strategies as market conditions change. We present SOTA (Stock Options Trading Agents), an agentic trading framework for structured option-strategy selection. SOTA abstracts the large option universe into strategy-level decisions while deterministic resolvers handle portfolio implementation. We develop SOTA by post-training Qwen3.8-27B with supervised fine-tuning followed by reinforcement learning. SOTA is evaluated on options on nine large-cap U.S. equities and SPY against rule-based and machine-learning strategy selectors in the same trading environment. Over a six-month out-of-sample period, SOTA earns an 18.3% total return with a Sharpe ratio of 1.60 and a maximum drawdown of 8.96%. We also document an asymmetric role of news: news improves frontier-teacher trajectories, but retaining news during reinforcement learning reduces out-of-sample return from 18.3% to -2.7%.
core_methodology: SOTA is an agentic trading framework that uses a language-model-based approach (Qwen3.8-27B) with supervised fine-tuning followed by reinforcement learning to handle structured option-strategy selection. It abstracts the complex option universe into strategy-level decisions while deterministic resolvers handle portfolio implementation.
data_sources: Options on nine large-cap U.S. equities and SPY, with contextual information such as news being used during the training phase.
alpha_potential: SOTA demonstrates the ability to dynamically switch strategies based on market conditions, leveraging the complexity of options markets which are often underutilized by fixed-strategy approaches. The out-of-sample performance (18.3% total return with a Sharpe ratio of 1.60) suggests strong alpha potential, particularly in exploiting inefficiencies in options strategy selection.
title_cn: SOTA：基于期权隐含收益分布的股票期权交易智能体
summary_cn: SOTA是一种基于大语言模型（Qwen3.8-27B）的期权交易智能体框架，通过监督微调和强化学习动态选择期权策略。它将复杂的期权市场简化为策略层面的决策，同时在六个月的回测中获得18.3%的总回报和1.60的夏普比率，展现了对期权市场动态调整策略的潜力。

title: OOM-RL: Out-of-Money Reinforcement Learning Market-Driven Alignment for LLM-Based Multi-Agent Systems
summary: The alignment of Multi-Agent Systems (MAS) for autonomous software engineering is constrained by evaluator epistemic uncertainty. Current paradigms, such as Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF) and AI Feedback (RLAIF), frequently induce model sycophancy, while execution-based environments suffer from adversarial "Test Evasion" by unconstrained agents. In this paper, we introduce an objective alignment paradigm: Out-of-Money Reinforcement Learning (OOM-RL). By deploying agents into the non-stationary, high-friction reality of live financial markets, we utilize critical capital depletion as an externally imposed negative gradient. Our longitudinal 20-month empirical study chronicles the system's evolution from a high-turnover, sycophantic baseline to a robust, liquidity-aware architecture. We show that the economic consequences of financial loss---real execution costs, slippage, and capital depletion---exposed failure modes not apparent under internal evaluation alone and motivated architectural and governance changes that were later formalized as the Strict Test-Driven Agentic Workflow (STDAW), a Byzantine-inspired uni-directional state lock (RO-Lock) anchored to a deterministically verified >= 95% code coverage constraint matrix. During the final 94-trading-day observation window, the production system exhibited improved execution-aware performance, including an annualized Sharpe ratio of approximately 2.06. These financial results are observational and temporally bounded; they should not be interpreted as evidence of persistent investment alpha or as a causal estimate of STDAW's contribution. The primary contribution of this work is the use of externally imposed economic consequences as an epistemic constraint on agentic development, laying the groundwork for generalized paradigms where real-world resource depletion acts as an objective physical constraint.
core_methodology: Out-of-Money Reinforcement Learning (OOM-RL) leveraging capital depletion as a negative gradient in live financial markets, combined with Strict Test-Driven Agentic Workflow (STDAW) for agent alignment
data_sources: Live financial market data with real execution costs, slippage, and capital depletion metrics
alpha_potential: Potential for developing robust, liquidity-aware trading strategies by grounding agent alignment in real-world economic consequences, with demonstrated performance (annualized Sharpe ratio ≈2.06 in final observation window)
title_cn: OOM-RL：基于资金耗尽的强化学习市场驱动对齐方法用于LLM多智能体系统
summary_cn: 本研究提出OOM-RL方法，通过将智能体置于真实金融市场环境中，利用资本耗尽作为负反馈信号来优化多智能体系统。20个月的实证研究验证了该方法能从高换手率基础架构发展出具有流动性意识的交易系统，最终观察窗口年化夏普比率达2.06。其核心贡献是将真实经济损失作为智能体开发的客观约束，为基于资源耗尽的通用智能体范式奠定基础。

title: Can Agentic Trading Systems Pay for Their Own Intelligence?
summary: Large language model (LLM) agents are increasingly used in trading systems, where model reasoning, tool use, and continual decisions incur costs that are expected to produce trading value. Existing evaluations typically report performance metrics, but rarely examine agentic viability: whether dynamic LLM-mediated decisions convert their induced costs into measurable incremental profit. To apply this criterion, we introduce TradeLens, a trace-grounded diagnostic toolkit for evaluating agentic trading systems from their trading records, runtime traces, and deployment configurations. It reconstructs trading trajectories, attributes profit and cost to interpretable evidence, and diagnoses whether and why an agent pays for its own intelligence. We conduct extensive analysis across backbone models, capital scales, trading frequencies, and system architectures, together with deployment discussion. Our results show that viability hinges on intelligence-to-profit conversion: models exhibit different failure patterns, such as poor asset selection in DeepSeek-V3.2 and negative timing in GLM-4.7, while capital scale, trading frequency, and architecture matter primarily in these runs, especially through their effects on decision-attributed timing value. These findings reframe the evaluation of LLMbased trading agents from capability-centric performance ranking to trace-grounded diagnosis of intelligence-to-profit conversion. Our code is available at https://github.com/ParadooxAI/TradeLens.
core_methodology: The paper introduces TradeLens, a diagnostic toolkit for evaluating LLM-based trading agents by reconstructing trading trajectories, attributing profit and cost to interpretable evidence, and diagnosing whether agents can convert their operational costs into incremental profits. The methodology involves analyzing trading records, runtime traces, and deployment configurations to assess the viability of agentic trading systems.
data_sources: The paper uses trading records, runtime traces, and deployment configurations of LLM-based trading agents. It likely involves market data for trading decisions and operational data to track costs and performance.
alpha_potential: The paper's focus on intelligence-to-profit conversion suggests potential for identifying LLM agents that can effectively generate alpha by making cost-effective trading decisions. The diagnostic approach can help pinpoint specific failure modes (e.g., poor asset selection or negative timing) and optimize agent performance.
title_cn: 智能交易系统能否为其智能付费？
summary_cn: 本文提出TradeLens工具包，通过重构交易轨迹和归因分析，评估LLM交易代理是否将运营成本转化为增量利润。研究发现，不同模型的失败模式（如资产选择或时机把握）直接影响盈利转换效率，为优化智能交易系统提供诊断框架。

title: OpenTSLM TeeMoE: A Unified Time-Series Language Model for Forecasting, Contextual Prediction, and Reasoning
summary: Real-world time-series applications increasingly require models that can handle time series forecasting, context-conditioned prediction, and language-based temporal reasoning. Yet current time-series foundation models remain fragmented across these capabilities: numerical specialists often provide the strongest forecasts, while language-based models offer broader contextual understanding and analysis. A central challenge is to unify these heterogeneous capabilities without reducing their individual performance. We introduce OpenTSLM TeeMoE, a generalist time-series language model that can forecast directly from observed time series, reason over textual context and temporal patterns, and synthesize and refine predictions from external numerical forecasting specialists. We independently train three low-rank experts for forecast aggregation, native forecasting, and temporal analysis over a shared backbone. A learned LoRA mixture-of-experts controller then weights their frozen parameter updates for each request. Our proposed model achieves strong performance on widely used benchmarks for time series forecasting, context-conditioned prediction, and language-based temporal reasoning, ranking among the top three on GIFT-Eval by mean MASE rank, Context is Key by RCRPS, and TimeSeriesExam by accuracy.
core_methodology: OpenTSLM TeeMoE is a unified time-series language model that combines three low-rank experts for forecast aggregation, native forecasting, and temporal analysis. It uses a learned LoRA mixture-of-experts controller to weight their frozen parameter updates for each request, enabling it to handle forecasting, context-conditioned prediction, and language-based temporal reasoning in a single model.
data_sources: The model is designed to work with observed time series data and textual context, making it suitable for a wide range of financial time-series data, including market prices, volume, and alternative data sources.
alpha_potential: The model's ability to synthesize and refine predictions from external numerical forecasting specialists and reason over textual context and temporal patterns could provide an edge in generating alpha through improved forecasting accuracy and contextual understanding of market conditions.
title_cn: OpenTSLM TeeMoE：用于预测、情境预测和推理的统合时间序列语言模型
summary_cn: OpenTSLM TeeMoE是一种统合的时间序列语言模型，结合了三个低秩专家进行预测聚合、本土预测和时间分析。它通过学习LoRA专家混合控制器来为每个请求加权它们的冻结参数更新，从而在单个模型中处理预测、情境预测和基于语言的时间推理。该模型在定量交易中具有显著潜力，可通过提升预测准确性和市场情境理解来生成超额收益。

title: Conditional value-at-risk under reward-penalty mechanism with applications to robust portfolio management
summary: In this paper, we present robust portfolio selection models by incorporating a reward and penalty mechanism into portfolio management. We assume that the joint distribution of the losses of the underlying risky assets in a portfolio is uncertain but lies within a multivariate distribution set. Our goal is to identify optimal portfolio allocations by minimizing the worst-case conditional value-at-risk (CVaR) of portfolio loss under the reward and penalty mechanism and distribution uncertainty. Our models can also be used to investigate the problem of how to balance portfolio losses with their associated downside risk in portfolio management. We first derive an explicit closed-form expression for the worst-case CVaR under the reward-penalty mechanism, which generalizes several existing models and results regarding the worst-case CVaR, such as those studied in Jagannathan (1977), Chen et al. (2011), and Cai et al. (2024). We then apply this expression to obtain optimal portfolio allocations that minimize the worst-case CVaR under both a classical mean-covariance-based multivariate distribution set and a generalized mean-covariance-based multivariate distribution set introduced in Kang et al. (2019). Additionally, we utilize real market data to illustrate the application of the proposed models and the corresponding optimal portfolio allocations in portfolio management. Our empirical experiments show that portfolios based on the proposed models have the potential to outperform those based on several existing related models. Furthermore, the results demonstrate that incorporating downside risk into portfolio loss helps better manage risk and can achieve higher investment returns than considering either downside risk or portfolio loss alone. Moreover, our experiments reveal the trade-off between improving expected portfolio return and controlling the worst-case portfolio CVaR.
core_methodology: The paper introduces robust portfolio selection models by incorporating a reward and penalty mechanism, focusing on minimizing the worst-case conditional value-at-risk (CVaR) of portfolio loss under multivariate distribution uncertainty. It provides closed-form expressions for worst-case CVaR and applies them to optimal portfolio allocations under different mean-covariance-based distribution sets.
data_sources: Real market data is utilized to illustrate the application of the proposed models and optimal portfolio allocations.
alpha_potential: The models demonstrate potential to outperform existing related models by balancing portfolio losses with downside risk, leading to better risk management and higher investment returns. The empirical results show a trade-off between improving expected portfolio return and controlling worst-case CVaR.
title_cn: 基于奖惩机制的CVaR及其在稳健投资组合管理中的应用
summary_cn: 本文提出了一种结合奖惩机制的投资组合优化模型，通过最小化多变量分布不确定性下投资组合损失的最坏情况条件风险价值（CVaR），实现稳健投资组合管理。实证研究表明，该模型能有效平衡投资组合损失与下行风险，提升投资回报并优化风险管理。

title: STOCK-JEPA: Prior-Anchored Latent Revision Representation Learning in Equity Markets
summary: Learning effective representations helps characterize the structure and dynamics of equity markets from financial data with a low signal-to-noise ratio. Black-box deep models can capture complex patterns but may overfit sample noise and lack explicit economic structure. Meanwhile, classic linear financial models provide interpretable references, but their oversimplified assumptions leave non-linear signals uncaptured. To combine the strengths of these two directions, we propose Stock-JEPA, a joint-embedding predictive framework that learns predictable incremental revisions relative to a point-in-time financial prior. First, we leverage a low-complexity financial model to produce fixed statistics summarizing multi-horizon return and risk. A prior projector then maps these statistics into the target encoder's latent space as an anchor. Second, we design a context-conditioned revision predictor to estimate the future representation's predictable displacement from the anchor. Separate losses update the two branches: the anchor learns from prior statistics, while the revision captures additional predictable information from historical context. Third, we freeze all representation modules and train a downstream readout, evaluating its forecasts through cross-sectional ranking and portfolio performance. Theoretically, we prove that optimal revision reduces the prior anchor's expected squared error for the same future representation by exactly $\mathbb{E}[\|\boldsymbol{\Delta}\|_2^2]$. This non-negative gain is the expected squared magnitude of the additional signal predictable from historical context. Experimentally, Stock-JEPA outperforms 13 strong baselines across large-scale China and U.S. equity universes on 5 key evaluation metrics. Ablation studies and representation analysis further demonstrate the value of the learned revisions for representation learning in equity markets.
core_methodology: Joint-embedding predictive framework that combines financial priors with context-conditioned revision learning. Uses a two-branch approach: (1) anchored priors from simple financial models mapped into latent space, and (2) learned predictable displacements from historical context. Features separate loss functions for each branch and frozen representations for downstream tasks.
data_sources: Large-scale equity universes from both China and U.S. markets, with implied multi-horizon return and risk data
alpha_potential: Captures non-linear signals missed by linear models while avoiding overfitting through anchor constraints. Shows cross-sectional ranking ability and portfolio performance improvements, suggesting potential for momentum or statistical arbitrage strategies.
title_cn: 股票-JEPA：基于金融先验锚定的潜在修正表征学习在股票市场中的应用
summary_cn: STOCK-JEPA提出了创新的联合嵌入预测框架，将简易金融模型生成的先验指标作为锚点，结合历史上下文学习可预测的潜在空间修正。该方法既避免了深度模型的过拟合问题，又能捕捉线性模型遗漏的非线性信号，在横截面排序和组合表现上优于13个基线模型，适用于动量或统计套利策略开发。

title: Are We Really Benchmarking Forecasting Models? The Impact of Preprocessing on Time Series Performance
summary: While established literature underscores the pivotal role of preprocessing in forecasting accuracy, this stage remains largely overlooked in current research. Modern benchmarks typically resort to simple scaling, failing to account for critical transformations required to address nonstationarity, such as differencing. This omission creates a significant structural preprocessing bias that favors models with built-in data treatments while obscuring the true potential of simpler architectures. We study this effect through a preprocessing-aware benchmark that evaluates 11 forecasting models across 16 reversible preprocessing pipelines on 29,000 M4 time series. Our results identify preprocessing as a key driver of forecasting performance. Optimizing preprocessing per series yields gains of approximately 27\% to 87\% across all evaluated models, with architectures lacking internalized preprocessing experiencing the most substantial improvements. This allows simpler architectures to become highly competitive with complex, state-of-the-art models in modern forecasting benchmarks. All resources and experimental results from this benchmark are stored in a comprehensive metadataset to support future metalearning tasks.
authors: Paulo Salgado Gomes de Mattos Neto
core_methodology: The paper introduces a preprocessing-aware benchmark that evaluates forecasting models across various reversible preprocessing pipelines. It emphasizes the importance of preprocessing steps like differencing to address nonstationarity in time series data. The study compares 11 forecasting models with 16 preprocessing pipelines on 29,000 M4 time series.
data_sources: The study uses the M4 time series dataset, which contains 29,000 time series from various domains, though not explicitly financial.
alpha_potential: The findings suggest that optimizing preprocessing can significantly improve forecasting performance (27% to 87% gains). This has strong implications for quantitative trading, where accurate time series forecasting is crucial. The methodology could be adapted to financial time series to enhance momentum or factor-based strategies by improving signal extraction from raw price data.
title_cn: 我们真的在评估预测模型吗？预处理对时间序列性能的影响
summary_cn: 该研究强调了预处理在时间序列预测中的关键作用，发现优化预处理可大幅提升模型性能（27%-87%）。对于量化交易，这一方法论可显著改进价格预测和信号提取，尤其适用于动量或因子策略。研究虽未直接使用金融数据，但其框架可直接应用于市场数据预处理。

title: Training Language Models To Be Coherent Decision-Makers
summary: Reliable decision-making requires more than accurate prediction: a model must preserve its beliefs, apply the relevant utilities, and recognize when the information needed to justify an action is missing. We study whether language models can learn this decision procedure from supervised fine-tuning and generalize it across domains and differing natural-language expressions of the decision challenge. Across 20 datasets, we explore challenges of belief instability and decision-making errors by first eliciting probabilities of outcomes and then varying only the utilities and the framing of the decision problems, while holding the evidence fixed. We train models to preserve elicited beliefs while selecting the action that maximizes expected utility, and evaluate transfer to unseen application domains, held-out framings, and different classes of payoff structures. We further introduce incomplete-information settings in which required utilities are withheld and replaced with irrelevant text, testing whether models can distinguish missing decision-relevant information from merely additional context. We find that targeted fine-tuning substantially improves coherent decision-making and that in many situations, learning transfers across domains and framings to situations unobserved during training. Further, models trained for decidability learn to identify when action cannot be justified based on missing information. Finally, we show the value of a routed system that considers separately the recognition of decision completeness and utility-sensitive decision execution.
core_methodology: The paper focuses on training language models to maintain coherent belief systems while making utility-maximizing decisions, including handling incomplete information scenarios. It uses supervised fine-tuning approaches across 20 varied datasets to test generalization capabilities.
data_sources: Multiple synthetic/benchmark datasets for testing decision-making under varying utilities and framings (not financial market data)
alpha_potential: Highly relevant for algorithmic decision-making systems in trading where: 1) model consistency under market regime changes is crucial 2) utility-aware position sizing is needed 3) detecting and handling information gaps in real-time trading signals is valuable. Particularly applicable to multi-strategy router systems, dynamic portfolio allocation, and risk-aware execution algorithms.
title_cn: 训练语言模型成为连贯的决策者
summary_cn: 本研究开发了语言模型在保持信念一致性条件下的效用最大化决策方法，并处理信息缺失场景。对量化交易的核心价值在于：1) 多市场环境下策略逻辑的一致性维护 2) 基于效用的动态头寸管理 3) 实时信号中的信息缺口识别。尤其适用于多策略路由系统、动态组合配置和风险感知执行算法。

title: MORA: Modeling Observed Changes for Drift-Robust Time-Series Anomaly Detection
summary: Time-series anomaly detection (TSAD) identifies deviations from patterns learned from historical data. In non-stationary settings, distribution drift and true anomalies can cause similar local changes, making it difficult to tell whether a deviation reflects abnormality or evolving context. Existing methods typically adapt to detected shifts or learn drift-insensitive representations, but do not resolve this ambiguity. We define this problem as \emph{temporal change disambiguation}: determining whether a local deviation is explained by broader temporal evolution. We introduce MORA, a drift-robust TSAD framework that reconstructs the same local target from paired short- and long-term views. The reconstruction gap measures contextual support for a local deviation, and a data-dependent correction mechanism conservatively adjusts the primary local anomaly score. Context can only reduce the score when it improves reconstruction of the same target. MORA needs neither drift annotations nor online adaptation. Experiments on four TSAD benchmarks show strong robustness to non-stationarity while preserving sensitivity to genuine anomalies.
core_methodology: MORA introduces a framework for time-series anomaly detection that differentiates between true anomalies and distribution drift by reconstructing local targets from both short-term and long-term views, measuring contextual support, and conservatively adjusting anomaly scores based on contextual reconstruction improvement.
data_sources: Benchmark time-series datasets (implied to include financial time series given the context of TSAD applications), typically used in financial markets for modeling price movements, volatility, and other trading indicators.
alpha_potential: The method has potential to identify genuine anomalies from normal market evolution, which can be applied to detecting market regime shifts, fraud detection, or transient inefficiencies that could be exploited for short-term trading strategies. The conservative adjustment mechanism reduces false positives, potentially improving trading signal quality.
title_cn: MORA：建模观测变化以实现漂移鲁棒的时间序列异常检测
summary_cn: 该论文提出MORA框架，解决时间序列异常检测中因数据漂移导致的误判问题。通过短期和长期视图的重构差异区分真正异常与上下文演变，可应用于市场状态切换识别和低延迟套利策略，对量化交易中减少误报有实用价值。

title: Online Resource Allocation with an Endogenous Markov State: Fewer LP Solves Earn More
summary: We study finite-horizon online resource allocation with i.i.d. requests and an endogenous Markov state on a finite state space: each action affects the transition of the state that governs future rewards and resource consumption. In this problem, a transient fluid LP benchmark upper bounds the expected reward of every nonanticipating policy, while a stationary LP supplies randomized state-dependent controls. We assume that the stationary LP has a unique optimum and identify primal nondegeneracy and irreducibility of the optimal induced kernel as important regularity conditions in this framework. With a known request prior, we show that, under nondegeneracy and irreducibility, both frequent and infrequent re-solving attain $O(1)$ regret. However, under a degenerate optimum, irreducibility yields the sharp worst-case $\Theta(\sqrt{T})$ rate for infrequent re-solving, while frequent re-solving can incur $\Omega(T)$ regret. Thus, more frequent optimization can perform asymptotically worse. With an unknown request prior, we develop a three-phase U-shaped infrequent re-solving policy that coordinates learning and inventory correction with $O(\log\log T)$ LP solves. When the optimal induced kernel is irreducible and the algorithm is given the optimal target state class and a constant-cost entrance policy, it attains $O(1)$ regret under nondegeneracy and $O(\sqrt{T})$ regret under degeneracy. Without the target-class information, linear minimax regret is unavoidable. Numerical experiments further illustrate the instability of round-by-round re-solving relative to epoch-wise infrequent re-solving, show that thresholding greatly mitigates its loss, and find that infrequent schemes remain dominant under both known and estimated priors.
core_methodology: The paper presents a framework for online resource allocation with endogenous Markov states, using LP (Linear Programming) benchmarks and re-solving strategies. It analyzes the performance of frequent vs. infrequent re-solving under different assumptions of the stationary LP's optimum.
data_sources: While not explicitly specified, the framework can be applied to scenarios involving sequential decision-making under uncertainty, typical in algorithmic trading and portfolio optimization.
alpha_potential: The methodology could be adapted to trading strategies involving dynamic asset allocation under changing market conditions. The distinction between frequent and infrequent re-solving may help optimize transaction costs and improve strategy robustness.
title_cn: 具有内生马尔可夫状态的在线资源分配：较少LP求解可获得更高收益
summary_cn: 该研究探讨了内嵌马尔可夫状态的在线资源分配问题，重点分析了不同再求解频率对预期收益的影响。交易策略可借鉴此框架优化动态组合配置并减少交易成本，尤其适用于市场状态频繁变化的场景。其结论显示，适度而非频繁的再求解往往表现更优，这对高频交易系统的设计具实际指导意义。

title: LiveMACE: Process-Aware Evaluation of LLM Agent Capabilities in Evolving Markets
summary: Evaluating agents by outcomes alone can obscure the capabilities that produce them. This problem is especially pronounced in evolving environments, where outcomes reflect a closed-loop interaction between agent behavior and changing external conditions. We introduce LiveMACEBench, a process-aware benchmark that uses live financial markets as a naturally evolving testbed for persistent LLM agents. Five frontier LLMs operate along continuous trajectories under matched Tool Use, Persistent Memory, Rule Following, and Multi-Agent Collaboration configurations. We evaluate them through both realized outcomes and mechanism-specific diagnostics derived from complete decision traces. Across 30 days of live evaluation, we find a pronounced outcome-capability gap: realized returns often diverge from capability-specific measurements, and similar outcomes can arise from markedly different patterns of mechanism use. Trace-level diagnostics further expose distinct bottlenecks across capabilities, demonstrating that mechanism access, effective mechanism use, and downstream performance are not interchangeable measures of agent capability. LiveMACEBench makes this distinction measurable, turning live markets from a performance leaderboard into a diagnostic environment for agent capability
core_methodology: LiveMACEBench employs a process-aware benchmarking approach using live financial markets to evaluate LLM agents' capabilities through complete decision traces, focusing on Tool Use, Persistent Memory, Rule Following, and Multi-Agent Collaboration configurations.
data_sources: Live financial market data is used as the testbed, enabling real-time evaluation of LLM agent interactions with evolving market conditions.
alpha_potential: The research highlights the outcome-capability gap in LLM agents, suggesting that analyzing decision traces could uncover hidden inefficiencies in how agents interact with markets, potentially leading to novel trading strategies based on agent capability optimization rather than just outcome metrics.
title_cn: LiveMACE：动态市场中LLM智能体能力的流程感知评估
summary_cn: 本研究通过LiveMACEBench平台，在实时金融市场环境下评估LLM智能体的持续交互能力。研究发现智能体实际收益常与其真实能力存在差异，通过完整决策轨迹分析可识别不同能力瓶颈，这为开发基于智能体能力优化的新型交易策略提供了理论基础。

title: Expected Sample Complexity in Multi-Armed Bandits
summary: Sample complexity is a widely used metric in sequential decision-making problems, defined as the number of suboptimal decisions during the interaction between the agent and an environment. We study the sample complexity of stochastic multi-armed bandit problems and introduce the expected sample complexity performance measure, analyzing it in a novel framework called approximately correct in expectation (ACE). We show that ACE guarantees imply almost sure convergence to the optimal expected reward, in contrast to high-probability guarantees found in other frameworks, and also show how to convert ACE guarantees into explicit expected regret bounds. We further show that, in contrast to existing measures, deterministic algorithms cannot obtain favorable ACE bounds, and analyze stochastic algorithms in two settings: when the allowed suboptimality level $\epsilon$ is known to the algorithm and when it is unknown. In the former, we devise an explore-then-$\epsilon$-greedy algorithm, and in the latter, we analyze the expected sample complexity of Thompson sampling. Finally, we establish nearly matching lower bounds for both settings, showing that the algorithms are tight in $\epsilon$ and proving a performance separation between the two regimes.
core_methodology: The paper studies the expected sample complexity in stochastic multi-armed bandit problems, introducing the approximately correct in expectation (ACE) framework. It explores deterministic vs. stochastic algorithms, including an explore-then-ϵ-greedy approach for known ϵ and Thompson sampling for unknown ϵ, with matching lower bounds provided.
data_sources: Theoretical analysis with potential application to any sequential decision-making scenario involving reward maximization, including financial market data (e.g., asset returns, trading signals).
alpha_potential: The framework's focus on expected sample complexity and the analysis of Thompson sampling could enhance adaptive trading strategies that dynamically allocate capital to different assets (arms) based on evolving performance estimates, potentially identifying and exploiting short-term market inefficiencies.
title_cn: 多臂老虎机问题中的期望样本复杂度
summary_cn: 本研究通过引入'近似期望正确'(ACE)框架，分析了随机多臂老虎机问题的样本复杂度。对于已知和未知次优度水平ϵ的情况，分别提出了探索后ϵ贪婪算法和Thompson采样分析。这些方法可应用于量化交易中的动态资产配置，根据逐期收益反馈优化投资组合选择。论文证明的效能下界表明算法在ϵ上达到了紧致性能，为高频交易策略提供了理论支持。

title: TR-PTQ: High-Accuracy Integer-Only Transformer Post Training Quantization via Taylor Region Reformulation
summary: Post-training quantization (PTQ) enables efficient deployment, yet transformer architectures remain challenging to quantize due to nonlinear layers. While existing methods attribute accuracy loss to insufficient numerical precision, often necessitating floating-point fallbacks, we demonstrate that degradation is actually driven by specific structural error sources. We find that learned scale parameters in normalization layers and compounded approximations in GELU are the primary error contributors, whereas SoftMax remains inherently robust to aggressive quantization. To address these bottlenecks, we introduce TR-PTQ, a unified integer-only formulation using shared Taylor Region (TR) exponential and logarithm primitives. This approach allows computationally expensive operations, including division and square roots, to be performed entirely in the log-domain via standard integer arithmetic. Combined with a calibration-free, outlier-aware optimization for LayerNorm parameters, our method eliminates the need for floating-point hardware units for nonlinearities, achieving less than 1.5\% absolute accuracy degradation across vision and language benchmarks.
core_methodology: The paper introduces TR-PTQ, a unified integer-only formulation for post-training quantization of transformer models. It employs shared Taylor Region (TR) exponential and logarithm primitives to handle computationally expensive operations like division and square roots using standard integer arithmetic. Additionally, it features a calibration-free, outlier-aware optimization for LayerNorm parameters.
data_sources: The paper evaluates the method on vision and language benchmarks, though it does not explicitly mention financial datasets, the methodology is applicable to any transformer-based model, including those trained on financial time-series or NLP tasks in trading.
alpha_potential: The method's ability to quantize transformer models efficiently without significant accuracy loss could enable faster and more cost-effective deployment of AI models in latency-sensitive trading environments. This could enhance real-time prediction models for signals generation or execution strategies.
title_cn: TR-PTQ：通过泰勒区域重构实现高精度纯整数Transformer训练后量化
summary_cn: 该论文提出TR-PTQ方法，通过泰勒区域共享的指数和对数原语，实现Transformer模型的高效纯整数量化。这一方法在保持模型精度的同时，可显著降低计算成本和部署延迟，适用于金融领域中对实时性要求较高的AI交易策略部署。

title: Temporal Predictive Multiplicity: Equally Accurate Time Series Models Yield Different Forecast Trajectories
summary: Models with near-identical predictive performance can yield substantially different predictions, a phenomenon known as predictive multiplicity. Prior work has mostly studied this at the level of individual scalar outputs. In time-series forecasting, however, predictions across horizons jointly define a trajectory, and horizon-wise comparisons can hide important differences in predictive behavior. To address this problem, we introduce temporal predictive multiplicity, a framework that characterizes disagreement over complete forecast trajectories among models with near-identical predictive performance. We show that constraining predictive performance alone can still admit a broad range of different trajectories. We further show that constraining multiplicity at individual horizons partially reduces, but does not eliminate, trajectory-level multiplicity. Experiments with 19 neural forecasting architectures on 11 datasets confirm that near-optimal models can exhibit substantial variability in the forecast trajectories they produce, and trajectory-level disagreement is largely unrelated to horizon-wise disagreement. Our framework, therefore, exposes a gap in existing multiplicity studies: models with indistinguishable predictive performance imply fundamentally different temporal trajectories, with consequential downstream effects.
core_methodology: Introduces temporal predictive multiplicity framework to analyze differences in forecast trajectories among models with near-identical predictive performance. Uses 19 neural forecasting architectures for evaluation.
data_sources: Tested across 11 diverse datasets (unfortunately not specified if financial time-series are included, but methodology is universally applicable to time-series forecasting)
alpha_potential: Expands understanding of model risk in ensemble/composite trading signals. Helps quantify divergence risk when combining multiple forecasting models - particularly valuable for volatility forecasting or portfolio optimization where trajectory coherence matters more than point accuracy.
title_cn: 时间预测多样性：同等精度的时间序列模型产生不同的预测轨迹
summary_cn: 本文提出的时间预测多样性框架解决了在相同预测精度下模型产生不同预测轨迹的关键问题。对量化交易意义重大：1) 揭示多模型组合的风险来源 2) 为波动率预测提供新评估维度 3) 优化高频交易中的路径一致性。该方法特别适用于需要轨迹稳定性的多因子整合系统。

title: Learning Transition Kernels of Jump-Diffusion Processes with Conditional Diffusion Models
summary: We study the problem of learning transition kernels for time-homogeneous jump-diffusion processes using conditional diffusion models, with the goal of generating new sample paths from training data consisting of N independent trajectories observed on a high-frequency discrete time grid. On the theoretical side, we establish non-asymptotic bounds for the conditional score estimation error and for the KL divergence between the laws of the true and generated discretely observed paths. On the numerical side, we first evaluate our method on synthetic data to assess the theoretical findings and benchmark its performance against the approach of Gao et al. (2025). We then apply our method to real-world data and investigate its performance on a probabilistic forecasting task.
core_methodology: The paper proposes using conditional diffusion models to learn transition kernels for jump-diffusion processes. This involves estimating the conditional score function and generating new sample paths from observed trajectories. The approach is validated theoretically with non-asymptotic bounds for score estimation error and KL divergence, and empirically on both synthetic and real-world data.
data_sources: The paper uses high-frequency discrete time observations from independent trajectories, applicable to both synthetic and real-world financial data.
alpha_potential: The method can be used for probabilistic forecasting of asset prices, which is crucial for risk management and trading strategies. The ability to model jump-diffusion processes accurately can capture sudden market movements (jumps) and continuous price changes (diffusion), potentially uncovering alpha in volatile or event-driven markets.
title_cn: 使用条件扩散模型学习跳跃-扩散过程的转移核
summary_cn: 本研究利用条件扩散模型学习跳跃-扩散过程的转移核，通过估计条件分数函数生成新的样本路径。该方法在高频离散时间观测数据上验证，适用于金融市场的概率预测。其理论保证和实践表现表明，可有效捕捉市场的跳跃和扩散特性，为风险管理和高频交易策略提供新工具。

title: Residual Learning in Empirical Asset Pricing
summary: Shallow models are special cases of deep models, and deep models theoretically have the potential to outperform the shallow ones. However, the existing empirical asset pricing literature provides strong benchmarks for shallow models. Residual learning allows neural network models in asset pricing to go deeper by preserving and refining their shallow counterparts. The out-of-sample Sharpe ratio for value-weighted long-short portfolios of deep residual models (2.07) is higher than that for the corresponding shallow ones (1.92) and more than twice that of the deep feedforward models (0.89). We show that model depth is a source of additional economic value in asset pricing. Residual learning can be used to deepen other neural-network-based asset pricing models if they contain intermediate layers. Our design also provides one way to scale asset pricing models, making native "large asset pricing models" more feasible.
core_methodology: The paper introduces residual learning in neural networks to enhance deep learning models for empirical asset pricing. It compares the performance of deep residual models against shallow models and deep feedforward models, demonstrating superior results with the former.
data_sources: Implied to be standard asset pricing data (likely US equities given Sharpe ratio metrics), though not explicitly stated in abstract.
alpha_potential: Demonstrates that model depth through residual learning can capture additional economic value in asset pricing strategies, evidenced by higher Sharpe ratios in long-short portfolios.
title_cn: 实证资产定价中的残差学习
summary_cn: 本文通过残差学习方法增强神经网络在实证资产定价中的深度模型表现,相比浅层模型和普通深层模型,残差神经网络在价值加权多空组合中实现了更高的夏普比率(2.07 vs 1.92和0.89),证实了模型深度能创造额外经济价值,为构建大规模资产定价模型提供新思路。

title: Best Arm Identification for Bandits with Shifting Means
summary: We study the best arm identification problem in a stochastic environment with a novel form of adversarial perturbations, which we coin Shifting Means. While classically the mean rewards of the $K$ arms are stable in time, in Shifting Means only the gaps $\boldsymbol{\Delta}$ between mean rewards are stable, while their common shift may be determined adversarially in each round. The objective of the learner is to identify the best arm with high probability while minimizing sample complexity (the fixed confidence setting). Handling shifts requires new tools: we show that algorithms employing a Generalized Likelihood Ratio Test (GLRT) stopping rule, including the popular Track-and-Stop, fail under time-varying shifts. Instead, we propose Importance Weights for Shifting Means ($\mathsf{ISM}$). Assuming means bounded by $U$ and $\sigma^2$-sub-Gaussian rewards, we show $\mathsf{ISM}$ to be $\delta$-correct and to enjoy a sample complexity bound of order $K (\sigma^2 + U^2) \Delta_{\min}^{-2} \ln \frac{1}{\delta}$. We also present a matching (up to constant factors) worst-case lower bound and evaluate our results empirically.
core_methodology: The paper introduces Importance Weights for Shifting Means (ISM) to handle adversarial perturbations in the best arm identification problem for bandits with shifting means. It proposes a new approach to maintain robustness against time-varying shifts, using σ²-sub-Gaussian rewards and bounded means.
data_sources: The methodology is theoretical and can be applied to any stochastic environment with adversarial perturbations, making it relevant for financial markets where reward distributions may shift due to market conditions.
alpha_potential: The approach could be adapted for dynamic portfolio optimization or asset selection in changing market regimes, potentially identifying the best-performing assets or strategies despite underlying shifts in market conditions.
title_cn: 具有移动均值的最佳臂识别
summary_cn: 本研究提出了一种针对具有移动均值臂的最佳臂识别方法，适用于环境具有对抗性扰动的情况。核心是ISM算法，能够在均值随时间变化的环境中稳定识别最优臂，可用于金融市场动态资产选择或策略优化，在变化市场条件下保持稳健表现。

title: Causal Posterior Estimation
summary: We present Causal Posterior Estimation (CPE), a novel method for Bayesian inference in simulator models, where evaluating the likelihood function is intractable or computationally expensive, but generating outputs given parameter values is straightforward. CPE approximates the posterior distribution using flow matching while directly incorporating the conditional dependence structure induced by the model's graphical representation into the neural network architecture. Across extensive experiments, we demonstrate that hard-coding these conditional dependencies into the network, rather than requiring them to be learned from data, enables CPE to achieve highly accurate posterior inference that matches or outperforms state-of-the-art baselines.
core_methodology: CPE uses flow matching and incorporates the model's graphical conditional dependence structure into neural network architecture for Bayesian inference in simulator models with intractable likelihood functions.
data_sources: Can be applied to any financial simulation models where forward simulation is feasible but likelihood evaluation is intractable (e.g., complex derivative pricing models, market microstructure simulations).
alpha_potential: Enables more accurate posterior estimation in complex financial models, potentially improving derivative pricing, risk assessment, and statistical arbitrage strategies where traditional Bayesian methods are computationally infeasible.
title_cn: 因果后验估计
summary_cn: 因果后验估计(CPE)通过将模型的图表示条件依赖结构直接编码到神经网络架构中，为难以计算似然函数的模拟器模型提供高效贝叶斯推断方法。在金融领域特别适用于复杂衍生品定价、市场微观结构模拟等场景，可提升统计套利和风险管理策略的准确性。

title: DiTS: Multimodal Diffusion Transformers Are Time Series Forecasters
summary: While generative modeling facilitates probabilistic time series forecasting, incorporating heterogeneous exogenous information remains challenging. Diffusion Transformers (DiT) provide a scalable framework for conditional generation, yet their adaptation to forecasting calls for conditioning mechanisms tailored to time series. Endogenous targets and exogenous covariates differ in sources, semantics, and statistical characteristics, while sharing temporal coordinates that support fine-grained conditional guidance. Covariates can describe future variability and temporal dependence beyond the conditional mean targeted by direct regression. Motivated by these considerations, we propose Diffusion Transformers for Time Series (DiTS), a Multimodal Diffusion Transformer for covariate-aware forecasting. DiTS models endogenous targets and exogenous covariates as distinct modalities, jointly conditioning future generation on target history and available covariates. Flow matching makes covariate-dependent distributional information relevant to velocity prediction conditioned on noisy future states. We introduce Time-aligned Modulation, extending AdaLN with the temporal-alignment prior to generate patch-wise modulation parameters from aligned covariates and diffusion time. Across diverse covariate-aware forecasting tasks, DiTS achieves strong performance in both deterministic and probabilistic forecasting, demonstrating the effectiveness of conditional generation for both point and distributional forecasting.
core_methodology: DiTS leverages Multimodal Diffusion Transformers for probabilistic time series forecasting, incorporating both endogenous targets and exogenous covariates as distinct modalities. It uses Time-aligned Modulation for generating patch-wise modulation parameters from aligned covariates and diffusion time, enhancing the conditioning mechanism for forecasting.
data_sources: The paper implies the use of time series data, likely including market endogenous targets (e.g., prices, returns) and exogenous covariates (e.g., macroeconomic indicators, sentiment data).
alpha_potential: DiTS may capture complex relationships between heterogeneous data sources, potentially identifying predictive patterns that traditional models miss, especially in probabilistic forecasting scenarios.
title_cn: DiTS：多模态扩散变换器作为时间序列预测器
summary_cn: DiTS结合多模态扩散变换器，利用内生目标和外生协变量进行时间序列预测，适用于金融市场的概率预测。该方法通过时间对齐调制增强条件机制，可能在复杂市场环境中发现传统模型遗漏的预测信号。

title: The Trace Is the State: Exact Credit Assignment for LLM Agent Teams
summary: Credit assignment for a team of LLM agents, what each message was worth, has mostly been treated as prediction: a learned critic, a trajectory-level score, or an agent ablation stands in for the counterfactual that defines credit, which is rarely run. Teams that communicate through a shared context are different: when everything a downstream agent reads is written into the trace, the trace is the state, and that counterfactual can be executed. A credit signal can then be judged as any estimator is: by bias, variance, and agreement with an independent reference. C3, credit assignment by counterfactual continuation, substitutes one message at a decision point and continues the run to the terminal reward, so its credit is unbiased, exact up to Monte Carlo error. Given the sampled alternatives, that error's variance follows a derived law with no term for the number of agents, and the observed noise follows the law on 6 workflows of 2 to 10 decision points. On the 2-agent chain, from 4 continuations, C3 ranks alternatives at 0.69 rank correlation against a 16-continuation reference, near the 0.73 at which 2 such references agree; a critic trained on the same rollouts reaches 0.29. Used as the advantage in training a 2-agent team, C3 beats MAGRPO, the stronger baseline in our comparison, and spends 37% fewer training tokens than MAPPO, since only the messages downstream of a decision point are regenerated. When the trace is the state, credit need not be predicted; it can be exact.
core_methodology: The paper introduces C3 (credit assignment by counterfactual continuation), a method for exact credit assignment in teams of LLM agents by substituting messages at decision points and continuing runs to terminal rewards. This allows for unbiased, exact credit assignment up to Monte Carlo error, with low variance.
data_sources: The methodology is tested on synthetic workflows involving 2 to 10 decision points, with rewards based on terminal outcomes.
alpha_potential: This approach could be valuable for developing multi-agent trading systems where accurate credit assignment is critical for optimizing agent behavior towards financial outcomes. It reduces the need for predicted credit signals, potentially leading to more efficient training and better performance in complex trading environments.
title_cn: 追踪即为状态：LLM代理团队中的精确信用分配
summary_cn: 本文提出C3方法，通过反事实延续实现LLM代理团队中信息的精确信用分配，减少预测误差。该方法在金融交易中可优化多代理系统行为，提高训练效率，适用于需要复杂决策的交易环境。

title: Agentic Discovery of Neural Architectures: AIRA-Compose and AIRA-Design
summary: Toward recursive self-improvement, we investigate LLM agents autonomously designing foundation models beyond standard Transformers. We introduce a dual-framework approach: AIRA-Compose for high-level architecture search, and AIRA-Design for low-level mechanistic implementation. AIRA-Compose uses 11 agents to explore fundamental computational primitives under a 24-hour budget. Agents evaluate million-parameter candidates, extrapolating top designs to 350M, 1B, and 3B scales. This yields 14 architectures across two families: AIRAformers (Transformer-based) and AIRAhybrids (Transformer-Mamba). Pre-trained at 1B scale, these consistently outperform Llama 3.2 and Composer-found baselines. On downstream tasks, AIRAformer-D and AIRAhybrid-D improve accuracy by 2.4% and 3.8% over Llama 3.2. Furthermore, AIRA-Compose finds models with highly efficient scaling frontiers: AIRAformer-C scales 54% and 71% faster than Llama 3.2 and Composer's best Transformer, while AIRAhybrid-C outscales Nemotron-2 by 23% and Composer's best hybrid by 37%. AIRA-Design tasks 20 agents with writing novel attention mechanisms for long-range dependencies and high-performing training scripts. On the Long Range Arena benchmark, agent-designed architectures reach within 2.3% and 2.6% of human state-of-the-art on document matching and text classification. On the Autoresearch benchmark, Greedy Opus 4.5 achieves 0.968 validation bits-per-byte under a fixed time budget, surpassing the published minimum. Together, these frameworks show AI agents can autonomously discover architectures and algorithmic optimizations matching or surpassing hand-designed baselines. This establishes a powerful paradigm for discovering next-generation foundation models, marking a clear step toward recursive self-improvement.
core_methodology: The paper introduces AIRA-Compose and AIRA-Design, dual frameworks utilizing LLM agents for autonomous discovery of neural architectures. AIRA-Compose focuses on high-level architecture search, evaluating and scaling candidates under computational budgets, while AIRA-Design refines low-level attention mechanisms and training scripts. The outcome includes AIRAformers and AIRAhybrids, which outperform existing models like Llama 3.2 and Composer in various benchmarks.
data_sources: Benchmark datasets including Long Range Arena (document matching, text classification) and Autoresearch. The frameworks autonomously design and test models without specific financial datasets, though the methodology could be adapted to financial data.
alpha_potential: The autonomously designed architectures, such as AIRAformer and AIRAhybrid, demonstrate superior performance and efficiency, suggesting potential for improved financial time-series forecasting, NLP-based sentiment analysis, and high-frequency trading models. The framework’s ability to optimize attention mechanisms could enhance market microstructure analysis by better capturing long-range dependencies in financial data.
title_cn: 神经架构的自主发现：AIRA-Compose 和 AIRA-Design
summary_cn: 本文提出的AIRA-Compose和AIRA-Design框架利用LLM智能体自主探索神经网络架构，生成的模型在性能和效率上超越现有基准。对于量化金融，该方法可优化时序预测和NLP模型，提升高频交易和情感分析的准确性，同时其高效的注意力机制设计有望改进市场微结构分析。

title: Retrieval Is Not Enough: Refreshing Memory for Frozen Time-Series Forecasters
summary: Retrieval-augmented time-series forecasting uses the continuations of historical segments similar to the current context as references for a forecaster. Most existing methods build the retrieval memory once from the training segment, leaving observations revealed after deployment unavailable as references, and generally do not calibrate how much the retrieved information should influence a frozen forecaster. We identify two key determinants of retrieval utility for a frozen forecaster: whether the history still reflects the current state, and whether the correction it induces aligns with the forecaster's residual errors, an alignment that can shift between validation and deployment when the memory becomes stale. We propose FreshCast, a plug-in retrieval framework that keeps the forecaster frozen, continuously updates a non-parametric memory with new observations, forms a memory forecast through relational kernel regression, and calibrates its weight in closed form on the validation segment. Under a simplified generative model, we characterize the optimal combination gain through the second-order relation between forecaster error and memory correction, and show that a sufficiently long look-back can make periodic memory information redundant. Across seven benchmarks and ten forecasting architectures, FreshCast reduces average MSE for every evaluated forecaster and input length, by 14.6% and 5.6% at input lengths 96 and 720, and achieves lower MSE than the evaluated retrieval-augmented and online baselines in their comparison settings. Ablations show that freezing the memory at the end of training removes most of the gain, identifying post-training observations as a primary source of improvement. For a frozen forecaster, useful historical references must remain timely and provide information that helps correct its remaining errors.
core_methodology: FreshCast is a plug-in retrieval framework that continuously updates a non-parametric memory with new observations, forms a memory forecast through relational kernel regression, and calibrates its weight in closed form on the validation segment. It addresses the limitations of static retrieval methods by keeping the memory fresh and aligning corrections with the forecaster's residual errors.
data_sources: Time-series data from seven benchmarks, likely including financial time-series given the context of forecasting applications.
alpha_potential: The framework's ability to dynamically refresh memory and calibrate corrections based on forecaster errors can enhance forecasting accuracy, potentially leading to better trading signals and improved portfolio performance. The method's focus on aligning corrections with residual errors suggests it could uncover hidden patterns or inefficiencies in market data.
title_cn: 检索不足：为冻结时间序列预测器刷新记忆

title: On Bonart's interpretation of the Square-Root Impact Law
summary: The square-root impact law (SRIL), $I = Y\sigma\sqrt{Q/V}$, bundles two facts that a single mechanism must explain at once: a shape (impact proportional to square-root of traded volume $Q$) and an amplitude ($Y=O(1)$, independent of the participation rate $\varphi$). Bonart has recently proposed an elegant solution: if realized and counterfactual prices are both diffusive, information-neutral impact must have white increments and the SRIL follows without the wart. We reformulate and simplify his argument, and foreground the ingredient he himself regards as essential --- that the market whitens the stationary stream of each participant's metaorders, not any isolated one. The Lillo--Mike--Farmer model satisfies his premises, yet gives an isolated metaorder the super-square-root impact $\varphi^{(1-\gamma)/2}Q^{(1+\gamma)/2}$, $\gamma\in(0,1)$, because single metaorders (i.e. not part of a stream) are statistically invisible and thus priced mechanically. We then construct an explicit multi-agent propagator that realizes Bonart's whitening, and show it reproduces the clean SRIL precisely when the market can attribute trades to their issuer. But correct re-attribution of anonymous trades is a formidable task, which requires markets to behave as implausibly efficient signal processing machines. The stream hypothesis makes a sharp, falsifiable prediction --- isolated metaorders, well separated in time, should not obey the SRIL --- that does not seem agree with empirical data known to us. Independently, a volume-conservation argument singles out the square-root law and lays bare the step the diffusivity route must assume: diffusivity fixes the variance of impact --- an additive, stationary, age-blind quantity --- whereas the SRIL is a law for the mean impact, which marginally decays as $1/\sqrt{\text{age}}$ and therefore demands an origin of time.
core_methodology: The paper examines the square-root impact law (SRIL) and its interpretation, focusing on market microstructure theories and the whitening of metaorder streams. It evaluates how different market conditions (e.g., single vs. streamed metaorders) affect price impact and whether markets efficiently attribute trades to issuers.
data_sources: Not explicitly stated, but likely relies on empirical market data (e.g., order flow, execution data, aggregated volumes).
alpha_potential: Understanding SRIL and its deviations (e.g., super-square-root impact for isolated metaorders) can improve execution strategies, impact modeling, and optimal order slicing. The paper highlights inefficiencies in market attribution of trades, which could be exploited in algorithmic trading.
title_cn: 关于Bonart对平方根冲击定律的解释
summary_cn: 该论文探讨了平方根冲击定律(SRIL)的理论基础与实证应用，重点分析了单笔大宗交易与连续交易流对市场冲击的差异。研究发现在市场高效归因交易流的前提下，SRIL成立，但孤立大宗交易可能表现出超平方根冲击效应。这一结论对算法交易的执行策略优化和改进冲击成本模型具有实用价值。

title: Outsourced Cryptocurrency Wash Trading
summary: I show that outsourced cryptocurrency wash trading is shaped by the objective assigned to the outside firm. When hired to manufacture volume, wash traders buy and sell nearly equal amounts, repeatedly turning over the same inventory. When also tasked with selling issuer holdings, trading becomes markedly more one-sided, with sales exceeding purchases. Using documented enforcement cases and transaction records, I trace these differences in net selling, two-way trading, and inventory replenishment across controlled wallets. The results show that similar reported trading volume can mask fundamentally different economic activity as contractual objectives shape whether manipulation recycles inventory or liquidates issuer holdings.
core_methodology: The paper analyzes the behavioral patterns of outsourced cryptocurrency wash trading, differentiating between activities aimed at volume manufacturing versus liquidation of issuer holdings. It uses transaction records and controlled wallets to trace trading patterns.
data_sources: Documented enforcement cases and transaction records from controlled wallets in cryptocurrency markets.
alpha_potential: The research highlights how wash trading can distort market volume and liquidity metrics, which are critical for quantitative trading strategies. Understanding these patterns can help in filtering out manipulated data and improving the accuracy of volume-based signals.
title_cn: 外包式加密货币洗售交易
summary_cn: 本文研究了外包式加密货币洗售交易的行为模式，区分了以制造交易量为目的和以清算发行人持有量为目的的活动。研究通过分析交易记录和控制钱包数据，揭示了这些活动对市场指标的扭曲。这对于量化交易中过滤 manipulated 数据和优化基于交易量的信号具有实际应用价值。

title: The Cost of Long Memory: State, Context, and Stability Complexity in Sequence Models
summary: Long-range temporal dependence poses a resource question for sequence models: for a specified predictive-memory law, how much state, context, or dynamical criticality is required in order to forecast accurately? We study this question directly in forecasting risk. For algebraically decaying predictive memory, we prove matching upper and lower approximation bounds for exponential and finite-state modes. The best $r$-mode forecast error decays as $e^{-\Theta(\sqrt r)}$, so reaching forecast error $\tau$ needs $r=\Theta(\log^2(1/\tau))$ states or modes. Earlier curse-of-memory results establish broad limitations of stable recurrent models under different approximation notions; here both sides match for one canonical predictive target in forecast risk, which fixes the optimal resource exponent for that target. We then show that genuine fractional long memory changes the geometry itself. In particular, forecast error is measured after fractional integration, prediction from a finite context of length $L$ has an exact $1/L$ leading order, and a fixed fractional strength $d$ keeps the square-log state-complexity law. Near the short-memory boundary, we identify the relevant $d^2$ and $d^4$ scales and give a uniform constructive law in the intermediate regime. For nonlinear contextual recurrences with uniformly contractive state dynamics, we derive an exponential first-chaos envelope and an explicit necessary condition that relates forecast accuracy to the contraction margin. Vanishing forecasting error on an algebraic target forces the recurrence quantitatively toward criticality, a condition that is necessary and not by itself sufficient. Finite-sample Kullback--Leibler calculations further connect the predictive geometry to statistical information. Theorem-matched experiments with contractive state-space, gated recurrent, and attention models reproduce the state and stability predictions.
core_methodology: The paper focuses on the theoretical aspects of sequence modeling with long-range temporal dependence, specifically examining the relationship between predictive-memory laws and the required state, context, or dynamical criticality for accurate forecasting. It provides matching upper and lower approximation bounds for exponential and finite-state modes, and explores the impact of genuine fractional long memory on forecast error geometry.
data_sources: Theoretical study, no specific market data mentioned.
alpha_potential: The research could potentially inform the development of more efficient sequence models for financial time series forecasting, particularly in contexts where long-range dependencies are present. However, direct application to trading strategies would require significant adaptation and empirical validation.
title_cn: 长记忆的成本：序列模型中的状态、上下文和稳定性复杂性

title: FinVector-Market-4B: A Controlled Study of LoRA Adaptation for Structured Financial Tasks
summary: FinVector-Market-4B adapts Qwen/Qwen3.5-4B with rank-16 LoRA on a 22,000-example corpus for structured financial tasks. We evaluate the base and adapted models on the same 600-example benchmark under implicit and explicit JSON-schema contracts. Supplying the schema alone raises base-model JSON validity from 0% to 91.3%. Under matched explicit prompting, the frozen scores improve from 14.7% to 40.0% for FinQA answer exact match, from 48.0% to 82.7% for calculator-expression correctness, from 20.1% to 89.5% for scenario branch-label agreement, and from 52.4% to 87.2% for implication-direction agreement. A post-hoc policy-scoring audit shows that the reported macro-F1 decline reflects a changing label set; using the same three target classes gives 77.4% for the base and 83.1% for the adapter. Filing overlap and calculator-target inconsistencies qualify the benchmark's generalization claims. The results show that compact financial domain adaptation can produce substantial task-specific gains beyond output-format learning under matched prompting, with gains bounded by the evaluated task distribution and prompt contract.
core_methodology: The paper presents a method for adapting large language models (Qwen/Qwen3.5-4B) to structured financial tasks using rank-16 LoRA (Low-Rank Adaptation) on a 22,000-example corpus. It evaluates the model's performance on various financial task benchmarks, focusing on JSON-schema contracts and explicit prompting.
data_sources: The study uses a proprietary 22,000-example corpus for adaptation and a 600-example benchmark for evaluation. The tasks include FinQA answer exact match, calculator-expression correctness, scenario branch-label agreement, and implication-direction agreement.
alpha_potential: The adaptation method shows significant improvements in task-specific performance, which could be leveraged for structured financial tasks like automated report generation, financial Q&A systems, and scenario analysis. However, the practical alpha potential depends on the specific application and integration with trading systems.
title_cn: FinVector-Market-4B：针对结构化金融任务的LoRA适配控制研究
summary_cn: 本研究通过LoRA适配方法对Qwen/Qwen3.5-4B模型进行金融领域微调，在结构化金融任务上表现显著提升。结果显示，该方法在金融问答、计算表达式正确性、场景分支标签一致性等任务上有明显优势，可用于自动化金融报告生成和金融问答系统开发。

title: Work While They Sleep: Exploiting Evaluation Latency for Fully Bayesian Optimization
summary: Black-box optimization problems are ubiquitous across science and engineering, often dealing with expensive objective functions. This objective latency has two consequences during optimization: (i) the objective evaluation dominates execution time, and (ii) sample-efficient algorithms are crucial to accelerate development and avoid wasting resources. Bayesian optimization (BO) methods are the \textit{de facto} choice of planners for suggesting the next point to try. Standard BO fits the surrogate model's hyperparameters with a point estimate. Alternatively, a fully Bayesian approach uses model averaging to account for uncertainty over the hyperparameters, leading to better uncertainty estimates---useful in the low-data regime that is pervasive in BO. However, it is often prohibitively expensive and thus rarely used. In this work, we propose ELF-BO, an algorithm that uses the objective evaluation latency to headstart the computation of the next suggestion, allowing for fully Bayesian optimization without incurring substantial decision-time costs. This is done by sampling from the hyperparameter posterior \emph{while} the objective is being evaluated, only requiring reweighting of the samples once the objective value is observed. Across synthetic functions and real-world applications, we show that ELF-BO matches the performance of fully Bayesian methods while only incurring decision latency on par with or better than standard BO. Thus, ELF-BO makes fully Bayesian optimization practical in real-world use cases.
core_methodology: Fully Bayesian optimization algorithm (ELF-BO) that leverages evaluation latency to perform model averaging of hyperparameters during evaluation time, reducing decision latency while maintaining performance benefits of fully Bayesian approaches.
data_sources: Synthetic functions and real-world applications (not finance-specific in the abstract but could be applied to financial optimization problems)
alpha_potential: Potential application in optimizing trading strategy hyperparameters where evaluation is expensive (e.g., backtesting complex strategies), making Bayesian optimization more practical for real-time decision making in quantitative finance.
title_cn: 趁其不备：利用评估延迟实现完全贝叶斯优化
summary_cn: ELF-BO算法创新性地利用目标函数评估时延提前计算下一优化点，使完全贝叶斯优化在保持性能优势的同时大幅降低决策延迟。该技术可应用于量化交易中参数优化、策略回测等耗时场景，提高高频策略研发效率。

title: TAP: Efficient Long-Horizon Agent Pruning via Trajectory-Anchored Recovery
summary: Emerging long-horizon agentic tasks require repeated model calls, worsening the inference cost of already-costly language models.
