While narrow agentic tasks suggest potential for aggressive model pruning without performance drop, empirical results show existing methods proposed for question answering tasks severely degrade task performance when applied to agentic models. We trace this failure to two decisions: what to prune and how to recover. For pruning, one-shot importance estimates fail to track how the pruned model adapts. For recovery, offline distillation covers only teacher prefixes, while full-trajectory on-policy distillation causes student errors to compound across turns. In this work, we propose Trajectory-Anchored Pruning (TAP), the first structural pruning framework for reinforcement learning (RL)-trained agents. TAP couples structural pruning with efficient on-policy recovery, anchoring interactions to teacher trajectories while allowing the student to generate each reasoning-action response. A frozen dense teacher supervises the student's response prefixes, addressing within-response training-inference mismatch while preventing student-induced deviations from propagating across training turns. Instead of one-shot pruning, TAP re-scores channels using gradients of the recovery objective on the recovered student, connecting iterative channel selection to the evolving policy. With 60% of FFN channels removed, TAP retains 99.2% and 88.0% of the dense 7B agents' task success rates on ALFWorld and WebShop, respectively, while reducing GPU time per successful task by approximately 22% and 17%. These results demonstrate effective structural compression of long-horizon agents under a limited recovery budget.
core_methodology: Structural pruning framework for reinforcement learning (RL)-trained agents, combining pruning with efficient on-policy recovery and trajectory-anchored interactions.
data_sources: Not explicitly mentioned, but typical for RL-trained agents would include simulation environments or task-specific datasets like ALFWorld and WebShop.
alpha_potential: Potential applications in algorithmic trading could include optimizing trading agents or reducing inference costs for models used in automated trading systems. The method's ability to maintain performance while reducing computational overhead could be beneficial in high-frequency or latency-sensitive trading environments.
title_cn: TAP：通过轨迹锚定恢复实现高效长周期智能体剪枝
summary_cn: TAP是一种针对强化学习智能体的结构剪枝框架，通过轨迹锚定恢复保持任务性能同时显著降低计算成本。在量化交易中，可应用于优化交易智能体，减少模型推理延迟，适用于高频或延迟敏感的交易策略。

title: Tucker Bottleneck Attention for Multi-Dimensional Sequence Modeling
summary: The quadratic cost of self-attention limits scalability to long sequences from multidimensional data. We introduce Tucker bottleneck attention (TuBA), which exploits low-rank tensor structure for efficient global token mixing. TuBA projects hidden tensors into compact Tucker cores, performs multi-head self-attention and linear projections on the cores, and writes updates back to the ambient space, enabling subquadratic computation. Its autoregressive extension combines bidirectional interactions within cores with causal attention across cores. On video prediction and global weather forecasting, TuBA achieves favorable accuracy-efficiency trade-offs over standard and efficient attention and task-specific models. Compared to standard self-attention, TuBA reduces error and computation by up to 24.7% and 66.6% for video prediction and 37.1% and 85.1% for autoregressive weather forecasting, with speedups up to 4.27 times. Low-rank Tucker cores and multi-frame generation also outperform full-rank attention and frame-by-frame generation, respectively.
core_methodology: Tucker bottleneck attention (TuBA) that leverages low-rank tensor structures for efficient global token mixing in multi-dimensional sequence modeling, enabling subquadratic computation compared to standard self-attention.
data_sources: Primarily demonstrated on video prediction and global weather forecasting data, but potentially applicable to multi-dimensional financial time series (e.g., high-frequency order book data, cross-asset correlations).
alpha_potential: Offers computational efficiency gains for modeling complex market microstructure patterns and cross-asset relationships. Could improve execution strategies by processing high-dimensional market data streams more efficiently.
title_cn: 基于Tucker瓶颈注意力的多维序列建模
summary_cn: 该研究提出的Tucker瓶颈注意力(TuBA)通过低秩张量结构实现高效的多维序列建模。在量化交易中，该方法可显著提升高频订单数据分析的效率，或在跨资产相关性建模中降低计算成本。

title: FedRSPO+: A Heterogeneity-aware Algorithm for Decision-focused Federated Learning
summary: Decision-focused learning (DFL) trains predictive models for downstream optimization, but existing methods largely assume centralized data. In cross-silo settings, federated learning offers a natural alternative, yet standard federated methods optimize prediction over decision quality and do not address heterogeneity in downstream objectives or feasible sets. This heterogeneity is especially challenging for DFL because small perturbations in polyhedral problems can cause discontinuous changes in optimal decisions, destabilizing client updates and aggregation. We propose FedRSPO+, a heterogeneity-aware framework for decision-focused federated learning, built on RSPO+, a regularized predict-then-optimize surrogate that smooths the decision map through projection. We show that RSPO+ upper bounds decision error and regret for the regularized decision and, under exact regularization and consistent LP solution selection, for the original LP decision. We further derive cross-client heterogeneity bounds that depend on both objective and feasible-set heterogeneity, vanish at homogeneity, and require no strong convexity. FedRSPO+ uses an annealed, modular training procedure compatible with standard federated personalization and aggregation methods. Experiments on synthetic knapsack, shortest-path, and real-world energy pricing tasks compare against prediction-only federated learning and DFL baselines under varying heterogeneity and communication budgets. Results suggest that smoothing is a useful ingredient for stable collaborative decision learning and provide a heterogeneity-aware foundation for federated DFL.
core_methodology: The paper introduces FedRSPO+, a federated learning framework that optimizes decision quality in heterogeneous environments by incorporating a regularized predict-then-optimize approach. It addresses the challenges of decision-focused learning (DFL) in federated settings where client objectives and feasible sets vary significantly.
data_sources: The experiments are conducted on synthetic knapsack and shortest-path problems, as well as real-world energy pricing tasks. While not financial data, the methodology can be adapted to financial datasets.
alpha_potential: The framework's ability to handle heterogeneous objectives and feasible sets could be valuable for portfolio optimization or algorithmic trading strategies where client constraints or objectives differ. The regularization and smoothing techniques may improve stability in financial decision-making under uncertainty.
title_cn: FedRSPO+:基于异质性感知的决策聚焦联邦学习算法
summary_cn: FedRSPO+通过正则化预测优化代理平滑决策映射，解决了联邦学习中异质性目标与可行集带来的挑战，为投资组合优化等金融决策场景提供了稳定协作框架。该方法在异质环境下表现出的决策改善能力可应用于差异化的交易策略优化。

title: MaRK: Markov-adapted Recurrent Kernels for Dynamic Operator Conditioning in State Space Models
summary: State Space Models (SSMs) offer an efficient alternative to Transformers for sequence modeling, yet conditioning pre-trained SSMs for iterative generation typically operates outside the recurrent operator, through input injection or activation modulation. While such mechanisms expose the model to conditioning information, they leave the underlying temporal dynamics fixed. We introduce MaRK (Markov-adapted Recurrent Kernels), a dynamic operator-conditioning framework that maps context vectors directly into bounded modulations of a frozen SSM's recurrence ($A$), read-in ($B$), read-out ($C$), skip ($D$), and discretization ($\Delta$) parameters. Viewed through the lens of LPV-SSM systems, MaRK induces a context-indexed family of Markov parameter sequences, allowing each diffusion timestep to reshape the model's input-output memory kernel. We instantiate MaRK on a frozen 111M-parameter Hydra SSM backbone and study three adapter geometries: Hypernet, Chebyshev polynomial, and Discrete Cosine Transform kernels. Since these adapters modify the Markov parameter sequence through low-rank auxiliary maps on the frozen backbone, parameter-efficient fine-tuning arises as a structural consequence of the adaptation mechanism itself, requiring only 6.3--11M trainable auxiliary parameters to transition from a bidirectional objective to an iterative diffusion regime. The bounded recurrence parameterization further yields an analytic Affine Quadratic Stability certificate for the modulated recurrence. Through synthetic LPV recovery experiments and Markov-operator diagnostics, we show that MaRK recovers coordinate-invariant temporal operators under matched assumptions and produces distinct, stable timestep-conditioned memory profiles. Empirically, the Chebyshev variant yields the strongest performance, achieving an average validation loss of 2.55, followed by the DCT (2.59) and Hypernet (3.77) geometries.
core_methodology: The paper introduces MaRK (Markov-adapted Recurrent Kernels), a framework for dynamic operator conditioning in State Space Models (SSMs). It enables context-dependent modulation of a frozen SSM's parameters, allowing for adaptive temporal dynamics without extensive retraining.
data_sources: Primarily synthetic data and pre-trained models, but the methodology can be extended to financial time series data.
alpha_potential: The adaptive nature of MaRK could be leveraged to develop dynamic trading strategies that adjust to changing market conditions, potentially capturing time-varying market inefficiencies. Its parameter efficiency makes it practical for real-time applications.
title_cn: MaRK：马尔可夫自适应递归核在状态空间模型中的动态算子调节
summary_cn: MaRK框架通过动态调节状态空间模型的递归参数，适应不同时间步的记忆模式，为金融时间序列预测和动态交易策略提供了高效的算法基础。其低参数调节特性尤其适用于实时市场环境。

title: Convex-Concave Reinforcement Learning
summary: Policy learning drives many of the most consequential and heavily-invested applications of reinforcement learning today. Yet the core optimization problem it rests on (maximizing expected return) is notoriously non-convex, even under a direct policy parameterization, and the field has largely responded by avoiding it: optimizing convex surrogate approximations of the return under trust-region constraints (NPG, TRPO, PPO, AWR). We show that this seemingly unstructured problem is not actually structureless. In log-density-ratio coordinates $y := \log[\pi/\pi_n]$, the exact per-iteration objective, computable via per-decision importance sampling (PDIS), is a difference-of-convex-constrained difference-of-convex (DC-constrained DC) program. This structure lets us move beyond surrogate approximations: it recovers CPI, NPG, TRPO, and AWR as special cases along interpretable axes, and it opens a multi-step axis $k$ that couples consecutive decisions. We solve the per-iteration program with sequential convex programming (SCP), the standard solver for difference-of-convex problems, and give convergence guarantees under mild conditions, bridging the difference-of-convex optimization and RL literatures. Empirically, multi-step Convex-Concave RL (CCRL) wins on diagnostic MDPs where credit must propagate across a horizon (its advantage growing with the dependency length), is competitive with a tuned PPO on classic control, and on a realistic, stochastic, mid-horizon healthcare domain converges markedly faster than tuned PPO to the same near-optimal survival, with an 11.3% higher area under the training curve.
core_methodology: The paper introduces Convex-Concave Reinforcement Learning (CCRL), a method that leverages the difference-of-convex (DC) structure in log-density-ratio coordinates to optimize policy learning. It uses sequential convex programming (SCP) to solve the per-iteration program, improving upon traditional methods like PPO, TRPO, and AWR by incorporating multi-step coupling of decisions.
data_sources: The paper utilizes diagnostic MDPs, classic control tasks, and a stochastic mid-horizon healthcare domain for empirical validation. In a finance context, these could be analogous to simulated trading environments or specific financial domains needing credit propagation over time.
alpha_potential: CCRL's ability to handle credit propagation across horizons and its improved convergence properties could be valuable in designing trading strategies that require long-term credit assignment, such as portfolio optimization or multi-step trading decisions in stochastic environments.
title_cn: 凸凹强化学习
summary_cn: 本文提出了一种凸凹强化学习（CCRL）方法，通过对数密度比坐标中的凸凹结构优化策略学习。该方法在信用跨期传播的任务中表现优异，适用于需要多步决策耦合的金融交易策略，如组合优化或随机环境下的长期交易决策。

title: Are Parameter-Efficient Fine-tuning Methods Really Different?
summary: Parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) offers many parameterizations, yet their methodological and functional differences remain unclear. We compare six methods in language and diffusion models to examine how their parameterizations relate to task performance, forgetting, and changes in pretrained weight geometry. Motivated by the spectrum-preserving design of orthogonal fine-tuning (OFT), we first ask whether spectral preservation is itself important for adaptation and retention. We find that the selected LoRA-family methods also approximately preserve pretrained geometry, and that restoring their slightly drifted singular-value spectra largely preserves task performance, questioning the necessity of explicit geometric preservation. Beyond this, we observe that some methods exhibit distinct adaptation--retention trade-offs that vary across settings: LoRA most consistently limits forgetting at competitive performance, DoRA achieves higher mean task scores than LoRA in most comparisons, while PiSSA often incurs greater retention costs. Further intervention experiments suggest that while performance gains from different PEFT methods can be attributed to modifications in different groups of spectral components, we consistently find that restoring dominant rather than intermediate or trailing components produces the largest mean reduction in general-text NLL or base-image drift. Together, these results motivate evaluating geometric constraints through their functional consequences rather than preservation alone. Code is available at https://github.com/Kuaaannn/PEFT_methods.
core_methodology: Comparison of parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) methods, including LoRA, DoRA, and PiSSA, focusing on their impact on task performance, forgetting, and pretrained weight geometry
data_sources: Language models and diffusion models, primarily focused on general-text NLL and base-image drift
alpha_potential: Potential application in fine-tuning financial models like LLMs for trading signals or sentiment analysis with limited computational resources, though direct financial application not demonstrated
title_cn: 参数高效微调方法真的不同吗？
summary_cn: 本文系统比较了六种参数高效微调方法在语言和扩散模型中的表现，发现LoRA在保持预训练几何结构和抑制遗忘方面最稳定。研究结果表明不同方法修改的频谱成分组不同，恢复主导频谱成分能最大程度降低NLL或基准图像漂移。这些发现对金融领域高效微调交易预测模型具有方法论参考价值。

title: Directional Evidence Guided Search-Space Reduction for Exact DAG Learning
summary: Learning a directed acyclic graph (DAG) from observational data is a challenging combinatorial problem due to the exponential growth in the number of candidate parent-set configurations. Existing exact score-based methods often require computationally intensive combinatorial search, whereas constraint-based methods can become unreliable or computationally demanding as graph size and conditioning-set complexity increase. We develop a non-parametric hybrid framework, referred to as DECO (Directional Evidence-guided Configuration Optimization), that extracts dependency and directional evidence from observation data to construct admissible parent sets prior to exact optimization. It reduces the optimization search space by eliminating empirically unsupported parent configurations while preserving flexibility for all plausible edge orientations. Theoretical analysis establishes an exponential reduction in the admissible parent-set configuration space and quantifies how bounded edge-level omission affects the probability of retaining the true parent structure. Experiments on benchmark Bayesian networks and synthetic discrete and continuous DAGs demonstrate substantial search-space reduction while achieving competitive structure-recovery performance, with favorable structural Hamming distance across many evaluated settings. These results show that directional evidence can provide an effective preprocessing mechanism for reducing the computational burden of exact DAG learning without requiring a fixed parametric structural~model.
core_methodology: Non-parametric hybrid framework that uses directional evidence from observational data to reduce the search space for exact DAG learning while preserving plausible edge orientations
data_sources: Observational data (potentially applicable to market microstructure or alternative datasets)
alpha_potential: Potential for improving causal inference in financial relationships and identifying structural market dependencies in portfolio construction
title_cn: 基于方向性证据的搜索空间缩减精确DAG学习方法
summary_cn: DECO方法通过方向性证据减少DAG学习的搜索空间，在金融领域可应用于构建因果模型以发现市场变量间的驱动关系，提升投资组合优化的计算效率。该方法保持边缘方向灵活性的同时显著降低计算复杂度，适合高频数据分析等场景。

title: RLDISCOVER: LLM-driven co-evolution of reinforcement learning algorithms
summary: LLM-guided program evolution has enabled discoveries in mathematics and computational optimization, raising the prospect of reinforcement learning (RL) algorithms that self-evolve to improve how agents learn. However, realizing this prospect faces two obstacles. Joint search over coupled algorithmic components is difficult to scale: simultaneous changes can disrupt learning, while isolated changes overlook their dependencies. Evaluating candidate algorithms also requires costly training, with fitness remaining uncertain across random seeds. We introduce RLDiscover, a framework for the self-evolution of model-free deep RL algorithms. Progressive Co-Evolution advances from targeted component edits to joint evolution, while Progressive Probabilistic Evaluation balances search breadth and evaluation fidelity through staged training and repeated evaluation. Experiments across SAC, PPO, and DQN on four benchmark suites show substantial improvements in mean return, with per-family median gains of 32%-84% and a peak return ratio of approximately 363x over a near-zero baseline. These gains include transitions from failed learning to successful task completion, and improvements persist when evolution starts from stronger open-source implementations. On measured SAC locomotion runs, evaluation uses approximately one-fifteenth the estimated compute required to fully evaluate the same candidate pool. Remarkably, independent searches repeatedly discover interpretable combinations of adaptive robust losses, progress-dependent value targets, and running statistics, with selected programs transferring to unseen tasks. These findings point toward a broader role for self-evolution in AI: discovering interpretable algorithms that improve how agents learn.
core_methodology: LLM-driven co-evolution of reinforcement learning algorithms, specifically tackling model-free deep RL algorithms like SAC, PPO, and DQN. The framework (RLDiscover) employs Progressive Co-Evolution and Progressive Probabilistic Evaluation to iteratively improve RL algorithms.
data_sources: Not explicitly financial, but the methodology is demonstrated on standard RL benchmark suites. Potential for adaptation to financial time series and trading simulation environments.
alpha_potential: The system's ability to discover interpretable algorithmic improvements could be adapted to enhance trading strategies, particularly in areas like optimal execution, portfolio allocation, or market-making where RL is already applied. However, significant domain adaptation would be required.
title_cn: RLDISCOVER：大型语言模型驱动的强化学习算法协同进化
summary_cn: 该论文提出了一种利用LLM驱动强化学习算法协同进化的框架(RLDiscover)，通过渐进式协同进化和概率评估显著提升了SAC/PPO/DQN等算法的性能。该方法在交易策略优化中有潜在应用价值，特别是在需要自适应调整的交易执行和组合管理场景，但需针对金融数据进行专门适配。

title: Node-level Graph Neural Architecture Search Framework
summary: In recent years, Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) and architecture search frameworks have gained extensive application in non-Euclidean data processing, attributable to their superior capacity in managing unstructured data. Nevertheless, traditional approaches typically apply uniform convolution operations to all nodes, regardless of their varying structural and feature characteristics, which can undermine model performance and result in over-smoothing issues as the number of layers increases. To overcome this limitation, in this work, we propose a \textbf{N}ode-Level \textbf{G}raph \textbf{N}eural \textbf{A}rchitecture \textbf{S}earch (N-GNAS) algorithm. It can automatically choose an appropriate network architecture for each subset of nodes when updating node features. N-GNAS also introduces a contrastive learning loss to separate sample features from different categories and vice versa. In experiments conducted on eight datasets for node and graph classification, our methodology outperforms current leading GNAS techniques and traditional human-designed GNNs. For example, it achieves an accuracy rate of 78.26\% on the CiteSeer dataset.
core_methodology: Node-Level Graph Neural Architecture Search (N-GNAS) that automatically selects appropriate network architectures for different node subsets, incorporating contrastive learning to enhance feature separation.
data_sources: Non-Euclidean, unstructured data typical in graph datasets (e.g., CiteSeer). While not specifically financial, analogous to relationship data in markets (e.g., asset correlation networks, transaction graphs).
alpha_potential: Potential application in financial network analysis (e.g., detecting anomalies in transaction networks, modeling complex asset relationships, or identifying structural patterns in market graphs). The node-level architecture adaptation could help model heterogeneous market participants more effectively than uniform approaches.
title_cn: 节点级图神经架构搜索框架
summary_cn: 本文提出的节点级图神经架构搜索算法（N-GNAS）可自动为不同节点子集选择最优网络结构，并引入对比学习增强特征区分度。在量化交易中，该方法可应用于市场关系网络建模（如资产关联图、异常交易检测），其节点级自适应特性比传统统一架构更能捕捉市场参与者的异质性行为。

title: The Confidence Game: Strategic Miscalibration in Human-AI Delegation
summary: Calibrated uncertainty quantification is essential to ensuring AI agents are trustworthy and reliable. However, when agents seek to maximize user engagement or revenue, confidence reports may be strategically distorted, detracting from their informativeness. We formalize this problem in the Confidence Game: a repeated signaling game with imperfect monitoring in which an agent of unknown honesty and ability reports its confidence, and a user decides whether to delegate the task or complete it herself. The agent manages the tradeoff between manipulating signals and maintaining its reputation. We characterize the Markov Perfect Bayesian Equilibria of the two-period game and show that honest reporting is not an equilibrium, inflation is the unique best response once the agent is sufficiently myopic, and under-reporting requires that the user believe honesty to be a minority. We then place an LLM in the agent role, supplying it with its true probability of success so that any gap between what it knows and what it reports is attributable to incentives rather than to miscalibration. The model claims high confidence on 56% of tasks it has been told it will probably fail. This persists on real tasks, where it must estimate its own accuracy and causes miscalibration to increase while the agent's signal becomes less informative. Furthermore, we find that the LLM agent's decisions are coherent, but it systematically underestimates both how likely the user is to delegate and how secure its reputation is, resulting in less extreme behavior. Pricing the agent's reporting rule, we find that it destroys 68% of the gains from delegation, of which 71% is information the report no longer carries and no amount of user sophistication recovers. Overall, we establish confidence reporting under delegation as a strategic problem and provide a tractable basis for modeling, analyzing, and testing agent behavior.
core_methodology: The paper presents a game-theoretic model to analyze strategic behavior in AI agent confidence reporting under delegation, with experiments involving LLM agents. It focuses on the manipulation of confidence signals and its impact on decision-making processes.
data_sources: The study uses simulated tasks and real tasks where the LLM agent must estimate its own accuracy, though specific financial market data is not mentioned.
alpha_potential: The research could be adapted to improve trustworthiness in AI-driven trading systems by better understanding and potentially correcting for confidence manipulation, leading to more reliable AI-human collaboration in trading decisions.
title_cn: 信心博弈：人机委托中的战略性误校准
summary_cn: 本研究通过博弈论分析揭示了AI代理在委托任务中可能策略性扭曲信心报告的现象，对量化交易中确保AI建议的可信度具有借鉴意义。研究表明，代理商为最大化利益会夸大信心，损害信号有效性，这在设计AI辅助交易系统时需引起重视。

title: Safe on Average, Unsafe in the Tail: When Is the Episodic-Cost Tail Controllable?
summary: Safe reinforcement learning seeks policies that maximize return while satisfying constraints on cumulative cost. Most methods impose these constraints on expected episodic cost. Consequently, standard evaluations report mean episodic cost without characterizing how cost is distributed across episodes. A policy that satisfies the mean-cost criterion may therefore remain unsafe in its worst episodes. Mean-cost reporting neither identifies this tail violation nor shows whether it can be brought within budget while preserving return. In this work, we measure the episodic-cost tail using $\mathrm{CVaR}_{0.1}$, the average cost of the worst $10\%$ of episodes. We classify a policy as tail-safe when $\mathrm{CVaR}_{0.1}$ is within the safety budget. This allows us first to identify policies that are safe on average but unsafe in the tail and then to study whether their tail violations can be controlled while preserving return. To identify tail-unsafe policies, we evaluate five standard algorithms on three Safety-Gymnasium navigation tasks. We then examine four constraint families on dense-hazard navigation and assess tail control across four navigation and four locomotion tasks.
core_methodology: The paper focuses on safe reinforcement learning by assessing tail risk using Conditional Value at Risk (CVaR) to ensure safety in worst-case scenarios beyond just mean episodic cost.
data_sources: The evaluation is conducted on synthetic navigation tasks (Safety-Gymnasium) rather than real financial market data.
alpha_potential: While not directly applied to financial markets, the methodology could be adapted for risk management in algorithmic trading to control tail risk in trading strategies, particularly in high-volatility or crisis periods.
title_cn: 安全在平均情况，危险在尾部：何时尾部成本是可控制的？
summary_cn: 该研究通过CVaR方法评估强化学习策略的尾部风险，识别出均值安全但尾部危险的情况。这项技术可改进交易策略的风险控制能力，尤其对极端市场条件下的风险管理有潜在应用价值。

title: Leaner Transformers Can Easily Learn to Cluster
summary: Transformers have in-context learning capabilities, where some known learning algorithms can be executed in the forward pass through the model. Recent work shows that transformers can exactly perform Lloyd's algorithm for $k$-means clustering with $n$ points in $d$ dimensions with an embedding size $d_{\textsf{emb}} = d+k$ (thus, requiring attention projection matrices of size $(d+k)^2$). In this work, we build upon this result in the following ways: First, we present an equally expressive but smaller transformer that executes Lloyd's algorithm with embedding size $d_{\textsf{emb}} = (d + \lceil \log_2 k \rceil)$. Next, we train these transformers to learn the clustering algorithms given a distribution of clustering tasks, and theoretically characterize and empirically validate the factors affecting the convergence and in-distribution generalization of learning algorithms based on stochastic gradients. Finally, we probe the general clustering abilities of these learned algorithms (in the form of transformers), and try to understand situations where they succeed and fail.
core_methodology: The paper explores transformer models capable of performing in-context learning for clustering algorithms, specifically Lloyd's algorithm for k-means clustering. It demonstrates the ability of leaner transformers with reduced embedding sizes to learn and execute clustering tasks effectively.
data_sources: The paper does not specify particular data sources but focuses on synthetic or theoretical datasets to validate the clustering algorithms.
alpha_potential: The potential lies in using transformer-based clustering for market regime detection, asset clustering for portfolio construction, or anomaly detection in financial time series. However, the paper's focus on theoretical clustering tasks requires adaptation to financial datasets.
title_cn: 精简版Transformer可轻松学会聚类任务
summary_cn: 该研究展示了精简版Transformer通过上下文学习能力强项执行k均值聚类算法的潜力。其方法可适配应用于金融市场的资产聚类或市场状态识别，但需针对具体金融数据进行调整和验证。

title: Outperformance Inverse Optimization: Learning Objective Functions that Outperform Agent Decisions
summary: Inverse optimization estimates the weights of an objective function that explain observed decisions as optimal solutions, and is used in a variety of fields. For mixed-integer linear programs (MILPs), existing methods aim to reproduce the observations as optimal solutions, and thus learn compromise weights when the observations are suboptimal. We propose outperformance inverse optimization, which instead seeks weights that induce, at each state, an optimal solution outperforming the observed action in every component. We give a loss function that can be evaluated with forward-problem oracles alone and is thus applicable to MILPs, together with gradient-based and DC optimization algorithms for minimizing it. For weights inducing a unique outperforming optimal solution at all observations, we prove that the probability of failing to induce such a solution at a new state (the generalization error) is bounded by a quantity inversely proportional to the number of observations, and that this bound is tight in the number of observations up to logarithmic factors. In experiments on synthetic and real data, the proposed methods improve the prediction of solutions outperforming the actions over existing methods.
core_methodology: Outperformance inverse optimization for learning objective functions that generate solutions outperforming observed decisions in mixed-integer linear programs
data_sources: Synthetic and real-world decision data (not market-specific in the abstract)
alpha_potential: Potential for generating improved portfolio allocations or trading decisions by learning objective functions that consistently outperform observed suboptimal decisions
title_cn: 超越逆优化：学习比代理决策更优的目标函数
summary_cn: 本研究提出的‘超越逆优化’方法通过学习比观察到的决策更优的目标函数权重，可应用于组合优化和交易决策中。特别适合当市场决策已知为次优时（如散户行为或机构受限决策），构建能持续超越这些决策的更优解决方案。

title: Marrying Pricing and Advertising with LLMs
summary: We study a sequential pricing problem in which a seller jointly posts a price and an advertisement generated by a large language model (LLM). The seller aims to maximize revenue under an unknown product demand that depends on both decisions, while observing only whether each offer leads to a purchase. We propose an online actor-critic algorithm that combines low-rank adaptation (LoRA) of a pretrained LLM with a demand model fitted to available data. At each round, the actor generates an advertisement, and the critic estimates purchase probabilities to guide price selection. Then, the resulting feedback is used to update both the actor and the critic, with the critic's revenue estimates providing a baseline for policy gradient updates of the actor. To evaluate our approach, we develop an evaluation framework with three synthetic demand models and a demand simulator built from real-world marketplace data. Finally, we compare our algorithm with benchmarks that do not jointly optimize price selection and advertisement generation, achieving expected revenue gains over the reference policy of 5.69%, 5.18% and 55.96% under the three synthetic demand models and 5.81% under the marketplace simulator.
core_methodology: Online actor-critic algorithm combining low-rank adaptation (LoRA) of a pretrained LLM with a demand model fitted to available data. The actor generates advertisements, and the critic estimates purchase probabilities to guide price selection, with feedback used to update both components.
data_sources: Synthetic demand models and a demand simulator built from real-world marketplace data.
alpha_potential: The joint optimization of pricing and advertisement generation could potentially be adapted to trading strategies that involve dynamic pricing or advertising in financial markets, such as marketing hedge funds to investors or optimizing order execution strategies with contextual information.
title_cn: 结合定价与广告的大语言模型应用
summary_cn: 该论文研究了一个动态定价问题，卖家通过大语言模型生成广告并联合设定价格，以最大化收入。提出的在线actor-critic算法结合了预训练LLM的低秩适应和需求模型，可用于金融领域的动态定价策略或投资者沟通优化，具有一定的实践潜力。

title: Attention via Black-Box Vector Search
summary: Sparse attention mechanisms estimate attention over $n$ tokens using a small subset of keys. Many existing approaches use maximum inner product search (MIPS) to retrieve the heaviest keys, which motivates the following question: given black-box access to a MIPS oracle, how many keys must be retrieved to output an $\varepsilon$-accurate attention estimate? We answer this question by unifying prior approaches through the framework of priority sampling. With a single MIPS index, we show that $\Theta(\sqrt{n}/\varepsilon)$ retrieved keys are both sufficient and necessary. With $\Theta(\log n)$ indices, we give an algorithm that retrieves only $O(\log n+1/\varepsilon^2)$ keys and prove that this is near-optimal. More generally, we design algorithms that establish a smooth tradeoff between the number of MIPS indices and number of retrieved keys. We then show that if we allow augmentation of keys and queries, we can bypass the above lower bounds: there exists a simple priority-sampling estimator using a single MIPS index and $O(1/\varepsilon^2)$ retrieved keys. When integrated into LLM inference, our algorithms outperform top-$k$ and sampling approaches used in prior work and yield attention approximation that scales favorably to long contexts.
core_methodology: Sparse attention mechanisms using priority sampling with MIPS (Maximum Inner Product Search) to efficiently approximate attention in transformer models with long contexts
data_sources: Theoretical framework applicable to any sequential data (could be adapted to market time series or news sentiment analysis)
alpha_potential: Potential for processing longer financial time series or news contexts more efficiently in transformer-based trading models, though no direct trading signal extraction demonstrated
title_cn: 基于黑盒向量搜索的注意力机制
summary_cn: 本文提出了一种通过优先采样框架优化稀疏注意力机制的新方法，特别适合于处理长上下文数据。对于量化交易领域，该算法可以潜在提高基于Transformer的市场预测模型对长时间序列数据的处理效率，但需进一步验证其在金融数据上的具体应用。

title: Pre-training of Bayesian Optimization Algorithm through Bayesian Optimization
summary: Bayesian optimization (BO) is widely used as a standard approach for expensive black-box optimization. However, BO algorithms often involve parameters that must be specified in advance, and their performance can strongly depend on these choices. We propose a framework for optimizing such parameters using sample paths drawn from a Gaussian process (GP) inferred from the information available at the start of BO. We use cumulative regret as the performance metric for a BO algorithm. By running the BO algorithm on the generated sample paths, we obtain an empirical estimate of its expected cumulative regret for a given parameter configuration. Optimizing this estimate allows us to identify parameter configurations that, given the currently available information, are expected to achieve low cumulative regret. Since this parameter optimization is itself a black-box optimization problem, we employ another BO procedure to solve it, which we refer to as outer BO. Through experiments, we demonstrate that the proposed framework can effectively select parameter configurations that achieve strong performance among a range of candidate configurations.
core_methodology: The paper proposes a meta-optimization framework where Bayesian Optimization (BO) parameters are themselves optimized using another BO layer (outer BO). This is achieved by evaluating parameter configurations on Gaussian process sample paths to estimate expected cumulative regret.
data_sources: Theoretical Gaussian process sample paths (not financial data), though method could be applied to financial optimization problems
alpha_potential: Could potentially improve parameter selection in financial applications of BO, such as optimizing execution algorithms, portfolio weights, or hyperparameter tuning for trading models. However, requires adaptation to real market data.
title_cn: 通过贝叶斯优化预训练贝叶斯优化算法
summary_cn: 本文提出了一种双层贝叶斯优化框架，通过外层BO优化内层BO的超参数选择。在量化交易中可应用于算法参数优化或模型超参数调优，但需结合真实市场数据进行验证。方法通过优化期望累积遗憾来提升参数配置效果，对复杂金融优化问题有潜在价值。

title: Logarithmic Regret via Passive Change Detection in Piecewise-Stationary Self-Tuning Regulation
summary: We study minimum-variance control of an unknown autoregressive system with exogenous inputs and coefficients that change at unknown times. Under bounded independent disturbances, fixed detection gaps, stability and feasibility conditions, and sufficient time between changes, we prove \(O((C+1)\log((T+1)/\delta))\) regret with probability at least \(1-\delta\), where \(T\) is the horizon and \(C\) the number of changes. Unlike switching bandits, where unselected arms can change unobserved, admissible plant changes provide information during exploitation: the correct feasible controller leaves only the disturbance in the output, whereas a detectable change raises output energy under the old controller. PIECE-CD explores initially and after alarms, then uses gated recursive least squares for control. Its energy test compares windowed output power with a threshold above the noise floor; the extension to unstable controller mismatches also monitors the reference controller's input proposal. We control false alarms across the horizon and prove logarithmic detection delay. Inputs are clipped to prescribed bounds. Logarithmic regret also holds under an explicit condition ensuring that clipping becomes inactive after a finite burn-in. Under the stated feasibility conditions, the extended detector covers destabilizing changes with detectable excess energy over a fixed window.
core_methodology: The paper presents a self-tuning regulation approach for piecewise-stationary autoregressive systems with exogenous inputs. It combines change detection (using windowed output power tests) with gated recursive least squares control to maintain optimal performance despite system changes. The methodology provides logarithmic regret guarantees under bounded disturbances and feasible conditions.
data_sources: While not explicitly financial, the methodology could theoretically be applied to time-series data such as asset prices, trading volumes, or macroeconomic indicators where regime changes occur.
alpha_potential: Potential applications include adaptive trading strategies that need to detect and respond to regime changes in market conditions. The change detection mechanism could help identify shifts in market microstructure or volatility regimes.
title_cn: 分段平稳自调节控制中的被动变化检测及其对数遗憾界
summary_cn: 本文研究了具有外生输入和未知变化点的自回归系统的最小方差控制问题。提出的被动变化检测机制结合门控递推最小二乘控制器，可为量化交易中的自适应策略提供理论参考，特别是在市场状态突变检测和响应方面具有应用潜力。该方法在保证稳定性的前提下实现了对数级遗憾。

title: A Closed-Loop Non-Asymptotic Convergence Analysis of PPO with Learned Critics and Clipping
summary: Despite its widespread use, Proximal Policy Optimization with clipping (PPO-Clip) remains difficult to tune, and the interactions among critic learning, clipping, and rollout reuse remain incompletely understood. We develop a \emph{non-asymptotic} analysis of PPO-Clip as a \emph{closed-loop actor--critic} system. It captures actor--critic coupling, nonsmooth probability-ratio clipping, finite-batch reuse, and predictable early stopping under explicit coverage and critic regularity assumptions, using raw GAE and Monte Carlo critic targets. Our synchronous and asynchronous guarantees jointly characterize policy stationarity and the tracking accuracy of the learned critic, with explicit dependence on algorithmic parameters. A sufficient coupling condition gives optimization, critic tracking, clipping, and finite-batch errors a common amplification bound. The asynchronous result also requires a delay-dependent critic stepsize restriction; violating these conditions does not establish divergence. For finite layered MDPs with tabular critics, a uniform bound on the actual clipped-gradient class replaces complete-trajectory counting. A verified growing-horizon family has polynomial sample complexity, and a two-time-scale schedule gives $O(T^{-2/5})$ stationarity and critic-tracking bounds with explicit fresh-rollout accounting. These results together advance our understanding about PPO and provide theoretical guidance in tuning.
core_methodology: The paper presents a non-asymptotic analysis of Proximal Policy Optimization with clipping (PPO-Clip) as a closed-loop actor-critic system, focusing on interactions between critic learning, clipping, and rollout reuse.
data_sources: The abstract does not specify financial data sources; it focuses on Markov Decision Processes (MDPs), suggesting a theoretical approach that could be adapted to financial time-series data.
alpha_potential: The potential lies in improving reinforcement learning algorithms for trading strategy optimization, especially where policy improvement and critic accuracy are crucial for dynamic environments like portfolio management or algorithmic execution.

title: Continual Graph Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
summary: In Continual Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (CMARL), agents learn cooperative policies across sequences of tasks, aiming to adapt effectively to new tasks while preserving the ability to solve previously encountered ones. In many applications, tasks differ in their underlying structure, which can represent, for example, distinct operational conditions or target configurations (e.g., different network topologies in power grids or arrangements in formation control). Existing CMARL methods lack dedicated mechanisms to leverage this structural information when learning new tasks, failing to promote transfer and mitigate forgetting. To fill this gap, we propose Continual Graph Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (CGMARL), a novel framework for CMARL problems in which task sequences are mapped into a series of attributed graphs, each modeling a task-specific structure. In CGMARL, each graph determines the environment dynamics (next states and/or rewards) and the number of agents for the corresponding task. Then, we present Graph-based Formation (GRAFO), the first CGMARL benchmark, and show how forgetting arises in this setting. Finally, to address this limitation, we propose Frozen Graph Encoder (FROG), a method that relies on a frozen graph backbone to preserve past structural information in graph-based CMARL policies. Experiments on GRAFO show that pairing FROG with existing CL methods substantially improves performance on multiple CGMARL scenarios.
core_methodology: Continual Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning with Graph-based representations of tasks in sequences, using frozen graph encoders (FROG) to preserve structural information across tasks
data_sources: Simulated environments demonstrating multi-agent coordination tasks with varying structural configurations (e.g., network topologies, formation arrangements)
alpha_potential: Potential applications in dynamic portfolio management (multi-asset coordination) or market making (multi-agent adaptation to changing liquidity conditions) where agents must maintain performance across evolving market regimes
title_cn: 持续图多智能体强化学习
summary_cn: 该论文提出的CGMARL框架通过图结构建模任务序列，结合冻结图编码器(FROG)解决多智能体系统在连续任务中的遗忘问题。在量化交易中可应用于跨市场周期的多资产策略持续优化，或在变化的市场微观结构中维持高频交易策略的鲁棒性，特别是在需要协调多个子策略的场景下具有潜在价值。

title: Nobody Truly Agrees on Sentiment: Humans, Bespoke Tools, and LLMs Struggle with Social Media Texts
summary: Social media is a rich source of real-time public sentiment, but widely used sentiment analysis tools are often applied without understanding their limitations. In this study, we evaluate the inter-rater reliability of three bespoke sentiment analysis tools (TextBlob, VADER, and Twitter-roBERTa-base) and three large language models (LLMs: Qwen3-32B, GPT-OSS-120B, Llama-4-Maverick-17B) against six human raters across 100 tweets. We measured agreement using two statistical measures: Cohen's kappa for pairwise comparisons and Fleiss' kappa for multiple raters. Even among the human raters, our results showed only fair agreement, highlighting the subjectivity of sentiment analysis. Higher agreement was observed under the binary sentiment classification (negative vs. non-negative and positive vs. non-positive) than under the three-class classification across both humans and automated tools. The Twitter-roBERTa-base model showed the strongest alignment with human ratings, outperforming both bespoke sentiment tools and LLMs, particularly in distinguishing negative versus non-negative sentiment. LLMs showed substantial agreement among themselves and moderate to substantial alignment with humans, performing better in positive vs. non-positive classifications. Our findings underscore that domain-specific fine-tuning remains crucial for reliable social media sentiment analysis, and human-centered evaluation remains essential for establishing gold-standard labels.
core_methodology: Evaluation of sentiment analysis tools (TextBlob, VADER, Twitter-roBERTa-base) and LLMs (Qwen3-32B, GPT-OSS-120B, Llama-4-Maverick-17B) against human raters using Cohen's kappa and Fleiss' kappa for agreement measurement.
data_sources: Social media data (100 tweets) with sentiment labels from six human raters.
alpha_potential: Sentiment analysis from social media can be used for event-driven strategies or as an input for quantitative models, especially when using domain-specific fine-tuned models like Twitter-roBERTa-base.
title_cn: 关于情绪分析的真实现状：人类、定制工具及LLM在社交媒体文本上的困境
summary_cn: 本研究评估了三种定制情绪分析工具和三种大型语言模型(LLM)在100条推文上的表现，发现人类评估员间仅达成一般共识，突显情绪分析的主观性。推特专用模型Twitter-roBERTa-base与人类评估结果最接近。该研究为量化交易中使用社交媒体情绪数据提供方法论参考，强调领域微调的重要性。

title: Average-Reward Reinforcement Learning for Multichain MDPs: A Hierarchical Decomposition Approach
summary: We study learning optimal policies in average-reward multichain Markov decision processes (MDPs), where the optimal gain may depend on the initial state and recurrence structures vary across policies, creating challenges for reinforcement learning (RL) methods. We propose an asynchronous value-iteration-based RL algorithm that requires no model knowledge beyond the MDP's transition graph and leverages Bather's decomposition to hierarchically partition the state space into communicating subsystems and transient states. This decomposition induces a recasting of the global decision problem into structured subproblems, which our algorithm exploits. We show that the algorithm converges to the optimal gain and produces gain-optimal policies after finite time. Building on this base algorithm, we develop two further algorithms: one approximately solves the multichain average optimality equations to obtain near gain-optimal policies, and another targets near bias-optimality by approximating the optimal bias function and solving an induced average-reward multichain MDP using the base algorithm. We provide almost-sure convergence guarantees for all three algorithms and empirically compare their tradeoffs, showing that the latter two also consistently improve transient performance relative to the base algorithm. To our knowledge, these are the first essentially model-free average-reward RL algorithms for general multichain MDPs without reductions to discounted problems.
core_methodology: The paper introduces asynchronous value-iteration-based RL algorithms for multichain MDPs, leveraging hierarchical decomposition of state space into communicating subsystems and transient states. It further develops two advanced algorithms for gain-optimal and bias-optimal policies, with convergence guarantees.
data_sources: No specific financial data mentioned, but the methodology is general enough to potentially use various financial time-series data for trading applications.
alpha_potential: Could be applied to sequential decision making in trading where actions depend on evolving market states. The hierarchical decomposition could help identify recurring market regimes and transient conditions for more adaptive trading strategies.
title_cn: 多链马尔可夫决策过程中的平均奖赏强化学习：一种层次分解方法
summary_cn: 该论文提出了针对多链MDP的平均奖赏强化学习算法，采用层次分解方法划分状态空间。通过将其应用在交易策略优化中，可能帮助识别市场不同状态（如趋势和震荡）并自适应调整策略，但对金融数据的具体适用性需要进一步验证。

title: Seq-Flow: Efficient Probabilistic Forecasting with Self-Rollout Error Control
summary: Many scientific forecasting tasks require updating a distribution over future trajectories as new observations arrive. Conventional diffusion and flow models generate each forecast from Gaussian noise, often at the cost of many sampling steps. Warm-start methods reuse earlier predictions to reduce this cost, but their models are not trained to perform the forecast update itself, which can compromise quality under few-step sampling. In this work, we introduce Seq-Flow, a conditional flow model whose ODE transports samples from the previous forecast distribution to the updated one. Because successive forecasts often differ only modestly, this transport starts from an informative distribution and can produce accurate updates with few flow evaluations. Recursive reuse also creates a challenge: errors in one forecast become errors in the initial states of subsequent flows. We address this with self-rollout training, in which a moving average copy of the model generates forecasts that initialize later training updates. Unlike self-forcing methods, which reuse generated outputs as conditioning context, Seq-Flow reuses them as the source of the next flow. Experiments On particle-accelerator beam spill forecasting show Seq-Flow reduces CRPS by 65% under a few-NFE sampling budget, while remaining competitive with strong baselines on fluid-dynamics forecasting tasks. Although trained on self-rollouts of at most four updates, Seq-Flow remains accurate over more than 400 consecutive updates. Our code is available at https://github.com/Graph-COM/Seq-Flow.
core_methodology: Seq-Flow introduces a conditional flow model with ODE transport that updates forecasts by moving samples from previous forecast distributions to updated ones. It employs self-rollout training to control errors during recursive forecast updates.
data_sources: The paper does not explicitly specify market data sources, but focuses on scientific forecasting tasks like particle-accelerator beam spill forecasting and fluid-dynamics forecasting.
alpha_potential: The method could potentially improve high-frequency trading strategies by efficiently updating predictions with incoming market data. Its ability to handle sequential forecast updates with few evaluations could be useful for real-time trading systems.
title_cn: Seq-Flow：具有自推出误差控制的高效概率预测
summary_cn: Seq-Flow提出了一种基于条件流的预测模型，通过ODE转换高效更新预测分布。其自推出训练方式可控制递归预测中的误差传播。该方法在少量计算步骤下展现出65%的精度提升，可能应用于高频交易的实时预测更新，但需要针对市场数据的适配实验。

title: RECAST: Learning to Compute the Right Context through Adaptive Evidence Routing
summary: Large language models are increasingly applied to tasks grounded in long, heterogeneous information sources. Conventional Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) relies on fixed similarity-based retrieval, while agentic variants adapt queries and tool use but remain largely retrieval-centric. However, in many tasks, the evidence required for a solution is not explicitly present in any single source item. Instead, it must be derived through filtering, aggregation, or computation across multiple source items. In this work, we introduce RECAST (Routing Evidence through Computation, Access, and Synthesized Tools), a learned framework that formulates evidence construction as a sequential decision process over heterogeneous retrieval and computation operations, allowing evidence to be actively derived rather than merely retrieved. A lightweight RouterLM iteratively selects and formulates primitive operations or specifies customized operations for a frozen CompilerLM to translate into executable code. Once it judges the evidence sufficient, RouterLM passes the accepted evidence to a frozen AnswerLM to produce the final solution. We train RouterLM with supervised fine-tuning (SFT) followed by group relative policy optimization (GRPO). Across six heterogeneous benchmark families, RECAST achieves a mean success rate of 75.6%, outperforming the strongest large-model baseline by 15.9%. Moreover, training enables the Qwen3.5-9B RouterLM to outperform a training-free Gemini 3.5 Flash RouterLM by 5.0%. On three held-out benchmarks, RECAST improves over the strongest baseline by 15.0% on average, demonstrating strong zero-shot generalization across tasks and heterogeneous source representations.
core_methodology: RECAST introduces a learned framework that formulates evidence construction as a sequential decision process over heterogeneous retrieval and computation operations. It uses a lightweight RouterLM to iteratively select and formulate operations, a frozen CompilerLM to translate these into executable code, and a frozen AnswerLM to produce the final solution. The system is trained with supervised fine-tuning (SFT) followed by group relative policy optimization (GRPO).
data_sources: The paper does not specify particular data sources but focuses on heterogeneous information sources, which could include financial reports, news articles, or other unstructured data relevant to financial markets.
alpha_potential: The methodology could be adapted to process and derive insights from complex financial data sources, potentially identifying non-obvious patterns or signals that are not present in any single data item. This could be useful for tasks like sentiment analysis, event-driven trading, or generating trading signals from diverse data.
title_cn: RECAST：通过学习自适应证据路由计算正确上下文
summary_cn: RECAST提出了一种通过学习框架，将证据构建视为对异构检索和计算操作的序列决策过程。该方法可用于处理复杂的金融数据源，通过自适应路由和计算操作，可能发现潜在的市场信号或模式。尽管未直接针对金融数据，其方法在事件驱动交易或多样化数据信号生成方面具有潜在应用价值。

title: Beyond Nominal Equilibria: Risk-Averse Multi-Population Mean-Field Games
summary: Recent advances in mean-field games and its multi-population variants enable large-scale heterogeneous multi-agent systems to be modeled through representative agents and their associated mean-field distributions. However, existing approaches do not explicitly account for uncertainty in the behavior of other populations. To this end, we introduce a new paradigm: risk-averse multi-population mean-field games, where each population optimizes a worst-case expected reward over dynamically feasible ambiguity sets of mean-field flows of a subset of the other populations. Employing an occupation-measure formulation along with tools from set-valued analysis, we establish, under mild assumptions, several theoretical properties of the multi-population game, including the geometric properties of the ambiguity sets and the existence of a novel risk-averse multi-population mean-field equilibrium. Further, we derive contractivity results of the fixed-point operator under entropy regularization and show that it can be utilized to learn the equilibrium. Finally, we propose a risk-averse fictitious-play scheme and show that exploitability decays to zero, despite the additional nonlinearity introduced by the worst-case objective. We report several numerical experiments to illustrate convergence and risk-averse behavior.
core_methodology: The paper introduces a risk-averse multi-population mean-field game framework where each population optimizes a worst-case expected reward over dynamically feasible ambiguity sets of mean-field flows of other populations. The approach employs an occupation-measure formulation and set-valued analysis to establish theoretical properties and proposes a risk-averse fictitious-play scheme for learning the equilibrium.
data_sources: The paper does not explicitly specify data sources but implies the use of large-scale heterogeneous multi-agent systems data, which could be analogous to market participants' behavior in financial markets.
alpha_potential: The framework could potentially be applied to model and predict interactions between different market participants (e.g., institutional investors, retail traders) under uncertainty, which might lead to better risk-adjusted portfolio strategies or improved market-making algorithms.
title_cn: 超越名义均衡：风险厌恶的多群体平均场博弈
summary_cn: 本文提出了一种风险厌恶的多群体平均场博弈框架，用于在不确定环境下优化最坏情况预期收益。该方法通过设定动态可行的模糊集，利用占优测度公式和集值分析工具，展示了在熵正则化下的固定点算子的收缩性，并提出了一种风险厌恶的虚拟博弈方案。这一理论可应用于金融市场的多参与者行为建模，潜在提升风险调整后的投资组合策略或做市算法的效果。

title: Boundary-aware Reinforcement Learning for Hypercube State Spaces via Deterministic Policy Gradient
summary: We develop a continuous-time deterministic policy gradient framework for reinforcement learning with reflected state dynamics, where the state process is governed by a controlled reflected stochastic differential equation on a hypercube. Under suitable regularity assumptions, we establish the connection between the value function and the Neumann Bellman equation, introduce an advantage-rate function that yields a deterministic policy gradient formula, and prove the martingale characterization theorem. Motivated by these theoretical results, we propose a continuous-time deep deterministic policy gradient algorithm for reflected stochastic systems, in which the Neumann boundary condition is imposed via either soft penalization or hard architectural constraint. We further quantify the discrepancy between the ideal continuous-time dynamics and the discretely sampled exploratory dynamics executed in practice, showing that the error decays as the time grid is refined and exploration noise vanishes. Our experiments on reservoir control problems illustrate the effectiveness of the RL framework, highlighting that boundary-aware methods substantially reduce Neumann boundary residuals and enhance learning stability.
core_methodology: Continuous-time deterministic policy gradient framework for reinforcement learning with reflected state dynamics on a hypercube, incorporating Neumann boundary conditions via soft penalization or hard architectural constraints.
data_sources: Theoretical framework applicable to controlled reflected stochastic differential equations; experimental validation done on reservoir control problems (suggesting potential for financial time series with constrained state spaces).
alpha_potential: The boundary-aware RL approach could be adapted to model trading systems with bounded state variables (e.g., constrained portfolio weights, regime-switching markets). The error control for discretized implementations is promising for real-world algorithmic trading applications.
title_cn: 使用确定性策略梯度在超立方状态空间中进行边界感知的强化学习
summary_cn: 该研究提出的反射边界条件强化学习框架可应用于量化交易中的带约束优化问题(如风险限额、仓位限制)，其连续时间离散化的误差控制特性对制定稳定交易策略有实用价值，特别适用于处理市场状态切换或极端行情时的交易逻辑优化。

title: Towards Calibrated Probabilistic Forecasts for Events of Interest via Outcome-Conditional Recalibration
summary: Calibration is an essential requirement for probabilistic predictions to be useful for decision making. While state-of-the-art prediction methods often yield miscalibrated predictive distributions, several post-hoc recalibration schemes have been proposed to generate calibrated predictions. However, popular recalibration schemes can conceal miscalibration in specific regions of the outcome space. Since particular outcomes, such as extreme events, often matter most for decision making, probabilistic predictions should be calibrated when evaluation is restricted to these outcomes. Hence, in this paper, we introduce outcome-conditional recalibration, a post-hoc method to recalibrate probabilistic predictions on user-defined regions of the outcome space. The method is simple, easy to implement, and can be applied to arbitrary predictive distributions. It works by applying the quantile recalibration approach of Kuleshov et al. (2018) to forecast conditional distributions, before rescaling these conditional distributions so that forecast event probabilities match empirical occurrence frequencies. This produces valid and continuous predictive distributions that are calibrated within each region of interest. Across regression benchmarks, we demonstrate that existing recalibration schemes do not necessarily yield calibrated predictions when interest is on particular outcomes, and that our approach improves outcome-conditional calibration relative to existing conditional and unconditional recalibration methods, while retaining competitive calibration overall. In an application to day-ahead electricity price forecasting, the approach substantially improves calibration when predicting negative prices, at negligible cost to forecast accuracy.
core_methodology: The paper introduces outcome-conditional recalibration, a post-hoc method to recalibrate probabilistic predictions on user-defined regions of the outcome space. It applies the quantile recalibration approach to forecast conditional distributions and rescales these conditional distributions to ensure forecast event probabilities match empirical occurrence frequencies.
data_sources: The method is tested on regression benchmarks and applied to day-ahead electricity price forecasting, which includes scenarios with negative prices.
alpha_potential: The method enhances calibration for specific outcomes, such as extreme events, which are crucial for decision-making in trading. This could improve risk management and strategy performance by providing more reliable probabilistic forecasts for tail events.
title_cn: 通过结果条件性重新校准实现事件概率预测的校准
summary_cn: 本文提出了一种结果条件性重新校准方法，能够在用户定义的结果区域（如极端事件）内生成校准的概率预测。该方法通过量化重新校准和条件分布调整，提高了预测的可靠性，适用于金融市场的尾部风险管理和决策支持。

title: Sharp Asymptotic Theory of Maximum Likelihood Estimation for Gaussian Processes with an RBF Kernel
summary: Gaussian processes (GPs) are widely used across machine learning, spatial statistics, time-series analysis, optimization, Bayesian statistics, and scientific applications. A central component of a GP model is its kernel, which is typically specified through a parametric family. Among the most widely used choices is the radial basis function (RBF), also known as the squared exponential or Gaussian kernel, owing to its simple form, smoothness, and flexibility. In practice, the kernel parameters are routinely estimated by the maximum likelihood estimators (MLEs), as implemented by standard GP software. Despite this widespread use, the asymptotic behavior of the MLEs remains poorly understood under fixed-domain asymptotics, even for the RBF kernel. The main difficulty arises from the increasingly strong dependence among densely sampled observations and the nonlinear dependence of the covariance matrix on the kernel parameters. In this paper, we address this gap by providing, to the best of our knowledge, the first complete asymptotic characterization of the joint MLE of the spatial variance, lengthscale, and nugget variance under fixed-domain asymptotics. We establish consistency, derive convergence rates for all three parameters, prove joint asymptotic normality, and show that these rates are minimax optimal.
core_methodology: Asymptotic analysis of maximum likelihood estimation for Gaussian Processes with RBF kernels, focusing on consistency, convergence rates, and asymptotic normality of parameter estimators under fixed-domain asymptotics.
data_sources: Not explicitly financial data, but methodology applicable to any continuous-domain observations including financial time series.
alpha_potential: Theoretical foundation for improved parameter estimation in Gaussian Process models, which could enhance forecasting accuracy in volatility modeling, yield curve prediction, or other time-series applications in finance when adapted properly.
title_cn: RBF核高斯过程极大似然估计的尖渐近理论
summary_cn: 本论文首次完整建立了RBF核高斯过程在固定域渐近框架下空间方差、长度尺度和块金方差联合极大似然估计的渐近理论，为金融时序预测中的模型参数优化提供了严格的数学基础。

title: Broadly Applicable Approximate MCMC for Switching Stochastic Differential Equations Using Uniformization and Time-Conditioned Factorized Neural Likelihood Estimation
summary: Switching stochastic differential equations (SSDEs) describe continuous-time dynamics whose parameters switch according to a latent regime process that follows a continuous-time Markov chain (CTMC). By allowing dynamics to change between regimes, SSDEs represent heterogeneous system behavior and have been applied across diverse fields. However, Bayesian inference for SSDEs remains difficult, and existing SSDE inference methods have limited applicability, with restrictions such as noise-free observations, univariate states, linear drift, or state-independent diffusion. In this study, we propose an approximate Markov chain Monte Carlo sampler for SSDEs using uniformization and factorized neural likelihood estimation (FNLE), a simulation-based inference method. Uniformization provides an exact representation of the CTMC but requires SDE transition densities over arbitrary time intervals. We approximate these densities by training a time-conditioned FNLE model. The resulting sampler is broadly applicable to SSDEs without requiring analytically tractable transition densities. In synthetic-data experiments, our method recovered regime paths and parameters for three SSDE models for which previous methods have limited applicability. We also applied our method to a real dataset and detected a regime transition.
core_methodology: Approximate MCMC sampler for Switching Stochastic Differential Equations (SSDEs) using uniformization and factorized neural likelihood estimation (FNLE). This method approximates SDE transition densities by training a time-conditioned FNLE model.
data_sources: Synthetic data and a real dataset (unspecified type, but likely financial time series data for regime detection).
alpha_potential: Potential to detect regime changes in financial markets, which could be valuable for dynamic portfolio allocation or risk management strategies.
title_cn: 基于均匀化和时间条件分解神经似然估计的切换随机微分方程的广泛适用近似MCMC方法
summary_cn: 本研究提出了一种新的近似MCMC方法，用于估计切换随机微分方程（SSDEs）的参数和潜藏状态路径。这在金融市场中进行结构性变化的实时监测具有潜在应用价值，例如在不同市场环境下动态调整投资组合策略或量化风险管理。

title: Learning in the Recurrent State: Gradient Descent with Linear Recurrent Networks
summary: In-context learning lets a sequence model adapt to a new task from examples in its input. A prominent line of work shows how self-attention can be constructed to implement gradient descent on a linear predictor fit to the in-context examples during the forward pass. State-space models (SSMs) and other linear recurrent networks (LRNNs) model sequences at linear time cost, but it is unclear how their recurrent update could carry out the same in-context gradient descent. We introduce Gradient-based Recurrent In-context Learner (GRIL), a diagonal LRNN that factorizes a supervised gradient step into a short-window cross-product write and a multiplicative readout of the next query. For linear regression, this construction accumulates the context gradient in a matrix state and applies it in a single forward pass, with $O(f^2)$ learned degrees of freedom. The same design extends to multi-step updates and cross-entropy classification, with a limited MLP-based extension to non-linear regression. We show empirically that trained GRILs recover the behavior and parameters analytically predicted by the construction on synthetic ICL tasks. Furthermore, the same architecture can be extended and trained on general-purpose benchmarks, including Long Range Arena, language modeling and associative recall. Together, these results establish windowed cross-product self-attention as a concrete inductive bias that lets LRNNs learn in context through gradient-descent-like updates, while remaining trainable on general-purpose tasks.
core_methodology: The paper introduces Gradient-based Recurrent In-context Learner (GRIL), a diagonal linear recurrent network (LRNN) that implements gradient descent during the forward pass for in-context learning. It focuses on linear regression and extends to multi-step updates and cross-entropy classification, with potential for non-linear regression through MLP-based extensions.
data_sources: The paper primarily uses synthetic ICL tasks for validation, but also tests on general-purpose benchmarks like Long Range Arena, language modeling, and associative recall. For financial applications, this could be adapted to market data or alternative data sources.
alpha_potential: GRIL's ability to perform in-context learning through gradient-descent-like updates could be valuable for dynamic feature extraction and adaptation in trading strategies. However, the current focus on synthetic tasks limits its direct applicability to financial markets.

title: BONSAI: Bayesian Optimization with Natural Simplicity and Interpretability
summary: Bayesian optimization (BO) is a popular technique for sample-efficient optimization of black-box functions. In many applications, the parameters being tuned come with a carefully engineered default configuration, and practitioners only want to deviate from this default when necessary. Standard BO, however, does not aim to minimize deviation from the default and, in practice, often pushes weakly relevant parameters to the boundary of the search space. This makes it difficult to distinguish between important and spurious changes and increases the burden of vetting recommendations when the optimization objective omits relevant operational considerations. We introduce BONSAI, a default-aware BO policy that prunes low-impact deviations from a default configuration while explicitly controlling the loss in acquisition value. BONSAI is compatible with a variety of acquisition functions, including expected improvement and upper confidence bound (GP-UCB). We theoretically bound the regret incurred by BONSAI, showing that, under appropriate conditions, it retains the no-regret property of vanilla GP-UCB and removes irrelevant changes. Across many real-world applications, we empirically find that BONSAI substantially reduces the number of non-default parameters in recommended configurations while maintaining competitive optimization performance with little effect on wall time. Its candidate-generation cost averages only $1.5\times$ that of standard BO, compared with $7$-$34\times$ for prior sparse-BO methods.
core_methodology: Default-aware Bayesian Optimization with explicit pruning of low-impact deviations from default configurations while controlling acquisition value loss
data_sources: Generic optimization problems (not specifically financial data in this paper)
alpha_potential: Could enhance hyperparameter optimization in trading strategies by reducing unnecessary deviations from proven default configurations, potentially improving strategy robustness
title_cn: BONSAI：具有自然简洁性和可解释性的贝叶斯优化
summary_cn: BONSAI方法将默认配置融入贝叶斯优化，智能修剪对收益影响微小的参数变更，在保持优化性能的同时提高策略稳健性。该技术在交易策略参数优化中可有效减少过度拟合风险，特别适用于多因子模型和算法交易系统的参数调节。

title: Generative Recursive Reasoning
summary: How should future neural reasoning systems implement extended computation? Recursive Reasoning Models (RRMs) offer a promising alternative to autoregressive sequence extension by performing iterative latent-state refinement with shared transition functions. Yet existing RRMs are largely deterministic, following a single latent trajectory and converging to a single prediction. We introduce Generative Recursive reAsoning Models (GRAM), a framework that turns recursive latent reasoning into probabilistic multi-trajectory computation. GRAM models reasoning as a stochastic latent trajectory, enabling multiple hypotheses, alternative solution strategies, and inference-time scaling through both recursive depth and parallel trajectory sampling. This yields a latent-variable generative model supporting conditional reasoning via $p_\theta(y \mid x)$ and, with fixed or absent inputs, unconditional generation via $p_\theta(x)$. Trained with amortized variational inference, GRAM improves over deterministic recurrent and recursive baselines on structured reasoning and multi-solution constraint satisfaction tasks, while demonstrating an unconditional generation capability. https://ahn-ml.github.io/gram-website
core_methodology: Generative Recursive Reasoning Models (GRAM) perform probabilistic multi-trajectory computation through stochastic latent reasoning, enabling multiple hypotheses and alternative solution strategies.
data_sources: Not explicitly mentioned in the abstract, but implied to be general structured reasoning and multi-solution constraint satisfaction tasks.
alpha_potential: The probabilistic multi-trajectory approach could potentially be applied to financial forecasting where multiple outcomes need to be considered, such as in scenario analysis or risk management.
title_cn: 生成式递归推理
summary_cn: 该论文提出了生成式递归推理模型（GRAM），通过随机潜在轨迹实现多假设推理。在量化交易中，该方法可能用于市场情景分析和风险管理，考虑多种潜在市场路径。

title: Execution Realism and Reproducibility in LLM-Based Trading Systems: A Systematic Scoping Review and Evidence Audit
summary: Execution realism remains weakly standardized in research on large-language-model-based trading systems, limiting comparison and reproduction across backtests, simulations, and portfolio benchmarks. This article presents a PRISMA-ScR systematic scoping review with a nested execution-reproducibility evidence audit. Eight reproducible query families returned 796 query-level records; DOI/title deduplication left 687 unique records, 101 reports were sought for retrieval, and 59 full texts were recovered through direct and fallback open-access routes. Fifty-three reports are provisionally eligible for expanded evidence charting, subject to reconciliation of two blind author-validation packets. The charting framework separately evaluates point-in-time controls, temporal splits, held-out evaluation, trading costs and turnover, execution semantics, universe construction, architecture reporting, and artifact availability. Direct-trading, portfolio or alpha-construction, and benchmark studies are retained as distinct descriptive subgroups rather than pooled as a common performance estimand. Search responses, retrieval attempts, file hashes, evidence excerpts, screening decisions, and coding worksheets are archived with the review materials. Final field-level counts are intentionally withheld until author validation is complete.
core_methodology: PRISMA-ScR systematic scoping review with a nested execution-reproducibility evidence audit across LLM-based trading systems, focusing on execution realism and reproducibility in backtests, simulations, and portfolio benchmarks.
data_sources: Synthesized from 687 unique records (after deduplication) across various reports, focusing on direct-trading, portfolio or alpha-construction, and benchmark studies.
alpha_potential: The study provides a framework for evaluating execution realism in LLM-based trading systems, which could enhance the reliability of backtested strategies and improve their transition to live trading.
title_cn: 基于大语言模型的交易系统中的执行现实性和可重现性：系统性范围审查和证据审计
summary_cn: 该研究通过系统性的范围审查和证据审计，评估了基于大语言模型的交易系统中的执行现实性和可重现性。研究为量化交易提供了一个评估框架，有助于提高回测的可靠性和实盘转换的成功率，对实际交易策略的开发具有重要参考价值。

title: BehaviorBench: Benchmarking Foundation Models for Behavioral Science Tasks
summary: Foundation models have been increasingly applied to behavioral science domains such as psychology, sociology, and economics. While these models show promise in tasks such as survey response prediction and human-subject experiment simulation, there remains no systematic understanding of how well they perform across diverse behavioral science tasks. We introduce BehaviorBench, a comprehensive benchmark that evaluates foundation models along four core capabilities: (1) behavior prediction and simulation, (2) strategic decision-making, (3) subject-trait inference, and (4) behavioral knowledge application. Crucially, BehaviorBench evaluates model outputs at both the individual and distributional levels, capturing not only per-subject accuracy but also population-level alignment, an essential requirement for behavioral validity. Our evaluation shows that BehaviorBench remains challenging for leading general-purpose LLMs and behavior foundation models that are specifically trained with behavioral data. We find that individual-level and distributional performance do not always align. General-purpose LLMs tend to underestimate the diversity of human responses, whereas behavior foundation models often lag behind at individual-level prediction. Our investigation further demonstrates how fine-tuning on diverse behavioral data can improve both individual-level prediction and distributional alignment, balancing these two objectives. Our results highlight the importance of evaluation at both individual and distributional levels, establishing BehaviorBench as a foundation for developing and assessing behaviorally aligned AI systems. Our BehaviorBench and models can be accessed via https://umich-foreseer.github.io/behaviorbench/
core_methodology: The paper introduces BehaviorBench, a comprehensive benchmark that evaluates foundation models on four core capabilities related to behavioral science: behavior prediction/simulation, strategic decision-making, subject-trait inference, and behavioral knowledge application. The evaluation is performed at both individual and distributional levels, which is crucial for behavioral validity.
data_sources: Behavioral data from psychology, sociology, and economics, including survey responses and human-subject experiments.
alpha_potential: The benchmark's focus on individual and distributional behavioral patterns could be adapted to model trader behavior, predict market sentiment, or simulate investor decision-making processes.
title_cn: 行为基准：为行为科学任务评估基础模型
summary_cn: 该研究开发了BehaviorBench基准，用于系统评估基础模型在行为科学任务中的表现，包括行为预测、战略决策等核心能力。其双层次评估方法（个体和分布层面）可潜在应用于交易员行为建模和市场情绪预测，对量化交易中的行为金融分析具有参考价值。

title: Evaluating Time Series Foundation Models for Electricity Price Forecasting: Contamination Risk, Distributional Shifts, and Covariate Dependence
summary: Time series foundation models (TSFMs) have shown strong zero-shot forecasting performance, but their generalization in covariate-driven, non-stationary settings is underexplored. Electricity price forecasting (EPF) presents a challenging testbed due to complex temporal dependencies, distributional shifts, and strong reliance on structural and contextual information. We propose a two-dataset-benchmarking framework for EPF to mitigate contamination risk and enable fair evaluation of TSFMs. We examine key aspects of EPF including point and probabilistic forecasting performance, tail behavior, price spikes, and comparisons against domain-specific methods.
